commit 3dd864cd8807b4dd975d563bde50056e9f85957a
Author: armel <armelhbobdad@gmail.com>
Date:   Fri May 15 15:04:06 2026 +0400

    feat(skf-setup): tighten headless contract, add CLI knobs, ship customize.toml
    
    Substantial quality pass on skf-setup that brings the skill to the
    Excellent grade per the bmad quality-analysis scanner:
    
    Headless contract:
    - Top-level status enum (success | tier_failure | write_failure | blocked)
      documented in the Invocation Contract and derived by the emit helper
      so pipelines branch on a single field.
    - emit-blocked envelope on every halt path (uv-missing, config-missing,
      config-malformed, three write-config failures). Halt-contract callout
      in On Activation stamps the two probe paths inline so the bootstrap
      halts can find the helper without first loading a reference file.
    - --orphan-action=keep|remove resolves the QMD orphan gate
      non-interactively, even outside --headless.
    - --ccc-skip-index lets operators with their own indexing schedule
      bypass the index build (envelope ccc_index.status="skipped").
    - --quiet suppresses the FORGE STATUS banner so expert re-runners
      and pipelines get the envelope only.
    
    Workflow shape:
    - Description quote closed (parser no longer truncates it).
    - Workflow Rules trimmed of restated baseline behaviors; Stages table
      drops the uniformly-Yes auto-proceed column.
    - On Activation collapses flag-parse into a single first step so every
      subsequent halt knows the mode.
    - Overview and Workflow Rules acknowledge --orphan-action alongside
      --headless as a gate-resolver.
    
    Determinism integration:
    - Stage prompts now consume helper-script outputs verbatim (effective_patterns,
      live_names, deltas, prior CCC fields) instead of re-deriving them in prose.
    - The detector reads forge-tier.yaml via --prior-state-from so stage 1
      no longer parses YAML; stage 1b reads previous CCC state from the
      detector's prior block.
    - The forge-data/ directory step now runs mkdir -p (idempotent) instead
      of an LLM-driven existence-check + branch.
    
    UX polish:
    - Opaque [BS]/[QS]/[AS] short codes in the closing banner replaced with
      the actual slash-command names users can type.
    - QMD-daemon-down case renders an explicit "QMD Registry: skipped"
      banner line instead of disappearing silently.
    
    Customization:
    - Minimum-three customize.toml (activation_steps_prepend / _append /
      persistent_facts) — the canonical landing for a deterministic
      system-executor workflow.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit 49937672b33f3f5552f4d32bc68cd513e9721450
Author: armel <armelhbobdad@gmail.com>
Date:   Fri May 15 15:03:10 2026 +0400

    refactor(shared/scripts): push deterministic operations into helpers
    
    Three helper scripts grew capabilities that previously lived as
    LLM-driven prose in step prompts, plus envelope assembly gained a
    single-field outcome enum and a bootstrap-safe blocked emit path:
    
    - skf-detect-tools.py accepts --prior-state-from and surfaces a
      'prior' block (previous_tier, previous_tools, previous CCC index
      state) plus a 'deltas' block (tools_added, tools_removed,
      tier_changed). Removes prose-side YAML parsing and set arithmetic.
    - skf-merge-ccc-exclusions.py resolves '{project-root}/...' template
      strings internally so callers forward raw config values verbatim,
      and returns 'effective_patterns' (the final sorted SKF pattern set
      after validation) so consumers no longer replay the ALWAYS_INCLUDE
      rules in prose.
    - skf-qmd-classify-collections.py invokes 'qmd collection list'
      itself instead of accepting pre-parsed names, and surfaces
      'live_names' so downstream callers don't re-fetch.
    - skf-emit-result-envelope.py adds a top-level status enum derived
      from existing error + require_tier_satisfied inputs, plus an
      emit-blocked subcommand that builds a minimal status="blocked"
      envelope from (phase, reason, optional path) with zero dependencies
      so early-halt paths (including uv-missing) can still emit.
    
    Schemas updated accordingly: SKF_SETUP_RESULT_JSON gains status
    plus ccc_index.status="skipped". 249 Python tests pass; test
    fixtures updated to match the new field shapes.

5	
6	# Agent Builder
7	
8	## Overview
9	
10	This skill helps you build AI agents that are **outcome-driven** — describing what each capability achieves, not micromanaging how. Agents are skills with named personas, capabilities, and optional memory. Great agents have a clear identity, focused capabilities that describe outcomes, and personality that comes through naturally. Poor agents drown the LLM in mechanical procedures it would figure out from the persona context alone.
11	
12	Act as an architect guide — walk users through conversational discovery to understand who their agent is, what it should achieve, and how it should make users feel. Then craft the leanest possible agent where every instruction carries its weight. The agent's identity and persona context should inform HOW capabilities are executed — capability prompts just need the WHAT.
13	
14	**Args:** Accepts `--headless` / `-H` for non-interactive execution, an initial description for create, or a path to an existing agent with keywords like analyze, edit, or rebuild.
15	
16	**Your output:** A complete agent skill structure — persona, capabilities, optional memory and headless modes — ready to integrate into a module or use standalone.
17	
18	## On Activation
19	
20	1. Detect user's intent. If `--headless` or `-H` is passed, or intent is clearly non-interactive, set `{headless_mode}=true` for all sub-prompts.
21	
22	2. Load available config from `{project-root}/_bmad/config.yaml` and `{project-root}/_bmad/config.user.yaml` (root and bmb section). If neither exists, fall back to `{project-root}/_bmad/bmb/config.yaml` (legacy per-module format). If still missing, and the `bmad-builder-setup` skill is available, let the user know they can run it at any time to configure. Resolve and apply throughout the session (defaults in parens):
23	   - `{user_name}` (default: null) — address the user by name
24	   - `{communication_language}` (default: user or system intent) — use for all communications
25	   - `{document_output_language}` (default: user or system intent) — use for generated document content
26	   - `{bmad_builder_output_folder}` (default: `{project-root}/skills`) — save built agents here
27	   - `{bmad_builder_reports}` (default: `{project-root}/skills/reports`) — save reports (quality, eval, planning) here
28	
29	3. Route by intent — see Quick Reference below.
30	
31	## Build Process
32	
33	The core creative path — where agent ideas become reality. Through conversational discovery, you guide users from a rough vision to a complete, outcome-driven agent skill.
34	
35	The builder produces three agent types along a spectrum:
36	
37	- **Stateless agent** — everything in SKILL.md, no memory, no First Breath. For focused experts handling isolated sessions.
38	- **Memory agent** — lean bootloader SKILL.md + sanctum (6 standard files + First Breath). For agents that build understanding over time.
39	- **Autonomous agent** — memory agent + PULSE. For agents that operate on their own between sessions.
40	
41	Agent type is determined during Phase 1 discovery, not upfront. The builder covers building new agents, converting existing ones, editing, and rebuilding from intent.
42	
43	Load `./references/build-process.md` to begin.
44	
45	## Quality Analysis
46	
47	Comprehensive quality analysis toward outcome-driven design. Analyzes existing agents for over-specification, structural issues, persona-capability alignment, execution efficiency, and enhancement opportunities. Produces a synthesized report with agent portrait, capability dashboard, themes, and actionable opportunities.
48	
49	Load `./references/quality-analysis.md` to begin.
50

54	
55	| Intent                      | Trigger Phrases                                       | Route                                    |

59	| **Quality analyze**         | "quality check", "validate", "review agent"           | Load `./references/quality-analysis.md`             |
60	| **Unclear**                 | —                                                     | Present options and ask                  |

63	
64	- **Analyze** — Run quality analysis: identify opportunities, prune over-specification, get an actionable report with agent portrait and capability dashboard
65	- **Edit** — Modify specific behavior while keeping the current approach

6	**Language:** Use `{communication_language}` for all output.
7	
8	# BMad Method · Quality Analysis
9	
10	You orchestrate quality analysis on a BMad agent. Deterministic checks run as scripts (fast, zero tokens). Judgment-based analysis runs as LLM subagents. A report creator synthesizes everything into a unified, theme-based report with agent portrait and capability dashboard.
11	
12	## Your Role
13	
14	**DO NOT read the target agent's files yourself.** Scripts and subagents do all analysis. You orchestrate: run scripts, spawn scanners, hand off to the report creator.
15	
16	## Headless Mode
17	
18	If `{headless_mode}=true`, skip all user interaction, use safe defaults, note warnings, and output structured JSON as specified in Present to User.
19	
20	## Pre-Scan Checks
21	
22	Check for uncommitted changes. In headless mode, note warnings and proceed. In interactive mode, inform the user and confirm. Also confirm the agent is currently functioning.
23	
24	## Analysis Principles
25	
26	**Effectiveness over efficiency.** Agent personality is investment, not waste. The report presents opportunities — the user applies judgment. Never suggest flattening an agent's voice unless explicitly asked.
27	
28	## Scanners
29	
30	### Lint Scripts (Deterministic — Run First)
31	
32	| #   | Script                           | Focus                                   | Output File                |
33	| --- | -------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- | -------------------------- |
34	| S1  | `./scripts/scan-path-standards.py` | Path conventions                        | `path-standards-temp.json` |
35	| S2  | `./scripts/scan-scripts.py`        | Script portability, PEP 723, unit tests | `scripts-temp.json`        |
36	
37	### Pre-Pass Scripts (Feed LLM Scanners)
38	
39	| #   | Script                                      | Feeds                        | Output File                           |
40	| --- | ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
41	| P1  | `./scripts/prepass-structure-capabilities.py` | structure scanner            | `structure-capabilities-prepass.json` |
42	| P2  | `./scripts/prepass-prompt-metrics.py`         | prompt-craft scanner         | `prompt-metrics-prepass.json`         |
43	| P3  | `./scripts/prepass-execution-deps.py`         | execution-efficiency scanner | `execution-deps-prepass.json`         |
44	| P4  | `./scripts/prepass-sanctum-architecture.py`   | sanctum architecture scanner | `sanctum-architecture-prepass.json`   |
45	
46	### LLM Scanners (Judgment-Based — Run After Scripts)
47	
48	Each scanner writes a free-form analysis document:
49	
50	| #   | Scanner                                     | Focus                                                                     | Pre-Pass? | Output File                             |
51	| --- | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------- | --------------------------------------- |
52	| L1  | `quality-scan-structure.md`                 | Structure, capabilities, identity, memory, consistency                    | Yes       | `structure-analysis.md`                 |
53	| L2  | `quality-scan-prompt-craft.md`              | Token efficiency, outcome balance, persona voice, per-capability craft    | Yes       | `prompt-craft-analysis.md`              |
54	| L3  | `quality-scan-execution-efficiency.md`      | Parallelization, delegation, memory loading, context optimization         | Yes       | `execution-efficiency-analysis.md`      |
55	| L4  | `quality-scan-agent-cohesion.md`            | Persona-capability alignment, identity coherence, per-capability cohesion | No        | `agent-cohesion-analysis.md`            |
56	| L5  | `quality-scan-enhancement-opportunities.md` | Edge cases, experience gaps, user journeys, headless potential            | No        | `enhancement-opportunities-analysis.md` |
57	| L6  | `quality-scan-script-opportunities.md`      | Deterministic operations that should be scripts                           | No        | `script-opportunities-analysis.md`      |
58	| L7  | `quality-scan-sanctum-architecture.md`      | Sanctum architecture (memory agents only)                                 | Yes       | `sanctum-architecture-analysis.md`      |
59	| L8  | `quality-scan-customization-surface.md`     | Customization opportunities and abuse; metadata validity                  | No        | `customization-surface-analysis.md`     |
60	
61	**L7 only runs for memory agents.** The prepass (P4) detects whether the agent is a memory agent. If the prepass reports `is_memory_agent: false`, skip L7 entirely.
62	
63	**L8 runs for all archetypes.** The scanner internally branches on `agent_type` to apply different rigor (metadata validity always; override-surface opportunities for stateless; sanctum-conflict detection for memory/autonomous).

66	
67	First create output directory: `{bmad_builder_reports}/{skill-name}/quality-analysis/{date-time-stamp}/`

73	uv run ./scripts/scan-scripts.py {skill-path} -o {report-dir}/scripts-temp.json
74	uv run ./scripts/prepass-structure-capabilities.py {skill-path} -o {report-dir}/structure-capabilities-prepass.json

78	```

81	
82	After scripts complete, spawn all scanners as parallel subagents.

84	**With pre-pass (L1, L2, L3, L7):** provide pre-pass JSON path.
85	**Without pre-pass (L4, L5, L6, L8):** provide skill path and output directory.

## Recommended approach (no internal-skill changes needed)

The existing `bmad-agent-builder` quality-analysis workflow at `.claude/skills/bmad-agent-builder/references/quality-analysis.md` **already orchestrates parallel subagents**: 2 lint scripts + 4 pre-pass scripts in parallel, then 6–8 LLM scanners spawned in parallel as Task subagents, then a synthesizer. That's the "genius" — it already exists. **No self-improvement of internal skills is necessary.**

The pattern that worked for `skf-setup` is:

```
1. fresh quality-analysis scan        (parallel inside the workflow)
2. triage findings → decision log     (you + me, conversationally)
3. apply fixes in one focused commit  (the equivalent of 3dd864cd)
4. one PR per skill                   (small, reviewable)
```

For the 3 remaining skills I'd suggest **one PR per skill, sequential** rather than batching. Reasons:
- Each elevation commit was substantial (`3dd864cd` was 9 files / ~280 lines). Three of those bundled would be a review nightmare.
- The skills share helpers but their headless contracts, halt paths, and customize surfaces are independent — there's nothing to gain from cross-skill batching.
- Each PR can land independently if one stalls.

**Parallelism opportunity (optional):** run the 3 fresh quality-analysis scans in **parallel via git worktrees** (one branch per skill). Scans are read-only and write to separate timestamped report dirs, so they don't collide. Triage + fix work then happens sequentially per branch.

I'd start with **skf-brief-skill** (smallest stale gap, freshest mental model). Invoke the analyzer on it, triage together, then apply the elevation commit.

## Grade tally

| Skill | Grade | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| **skf-brief-skill** | Excellent ✅ | Already there. Customize-surface gap + 3 enhancements only. |
| **skf-create-skill** | **Good** ⬆️ | Still needs lifting. ~3 HIGH items. |

Two of three are **already Excellent** thanks to PR #305's module-wide refactor + shared scripts. Only `skf-create-skill` needs lifting to match.

## Shared themes (apply uniformly across all 3)

| # | Theme | Severity | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|
| **S1** | Ship `customize.toml` minimum-three + `[agent]` metadata block (all 3 missing) | HIGH | small |
| **S2** | Repo-hygiene: scrub stale `.analysis/` dirs inside `src/skf-*-skill/` (causing false-positive lint findings + noise) | repo-hygiene | trivial |
| **S3** | Extract **Description Guard** into shared script (duplicated in create + update) | HIGH | medium |

## Skill-specific findings

**skf-create-skill** (the one lifting to Excellent):
- C1. Path-standards in stage files: parent-dir frontmatter refs in `references/sub/{ccc-discover,fetch-docs}.md`, `~/.skf/workspace/` literal in `source-resolution-protocols.md`, missing `{communication_language}` config header in 14 stage files — **HIGH**
- C2. Script extraction: `extract.md §4c` (script/asset detection), `extract.md §2a` (authoritative-files protocol), `load-brief.md §3` (brief schema validation) — **HIGH**
- C3. Carve `extract.md §2a` to own protocol file (379→~285 lines) — medium
- C4. Parallelize `fetch-temporal.md §3` (4 gh calls) + `fetch-docs.md §3` (up to 10 subpages) — medium, 5–18s wall-clock
- C5. Per-gate headless overrides via `[agent.gate_defaults]` — medium (depends on S1)
- C6. UX polish: rename leaves orphans, version-overwrite no diff, Quick-tier doesn't suggest upgrade — medium

**skf-update-skill** (already Excellent):
- U1. 5 more script extractions: change-manifest builder, provenance gap-driven dispatcher, SHA-256 hashing, workspace-drift git guard, atomic symlink update — HIGH
- U2. Headless observability: `headless_decisions[]` in result contract, `--dry-run`, `--detect-only` — medium
- U3. Concurrency lock (prevent corrupted provenance from simultaneous runs) — medium
- U4. Document cross-skill data coupling in `## Conventions` (re-extract.md pulls from create-skill/references/) — low

**skf-brief-skill** (already Excellent):
- B1. Lift 3 asset paths to `customize.toml` scalars (`description_voice_examples_path`, `scope_templates_path`, `brief_schema_path`) — medium
- B2. "brief from preset" interactive entry — medium
- B3. "preview create-skill output" between confirm + write — medium
- B4. Spec/remove workspace-list `'list'` pagination at step 2 §1b — low
- B5. `skf-count-sentences.py` helper (~150 tok/run) — low
- B6. Promote "wanted something different?" cancel line — low

## Recommended scope for one PR

**Core (must-have for elevation symmetry):** S1, S2, S3, C1, C2, U1

That's the equivalent of skf-setup's commit `3dd864cd` × 3 + shared-helper commit + repo-hygiene commit. Lifts create-skill to Excellent and matches setup's depth across the board.

**Stretch (if appetite is there):** C3, C4, C5, U2, U3, B1

**Defer to follow-up:** C6, U4, B2–B6 (these are real but cosmetic/UX — better as separate stories so the PR stays reviewable)

> AGENT

The Description Guard is a 4-phase **protocol** woven across multiple tool calls (capture before tool, verify+restore after). The deterministic parts (capture, hash-compare, restore) are extractable into a script with `capture` and `verify-restore` subcommands; the prose protocol could move to a shared reference doc.

Before I keep digging, let me give you a level-set on what I've learned:

## Honest scope assessment

After discovery, **"Everything"** breaks down differently than the headline:

| Category | Items | Confidence | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Deterministic script extractions** | 9 scripts (S3, U1×5, C2×3) | HIGH — clear inputs/outputs | Ready to build |
| **customize.toml × 3** (S1) | 3 files mirroring skf-setup | HIGH — pattern exists | Ready to ship |
| **Path-standards fixes in create-skill** (C1) | ~14 stage files | HIGH — mechanical | Ready to ship |
| **Carve extract.md §2a** (C3) | 1 file split | HIGH | Ready to ship |
| **Parallelize fetch-temporal/fetch-docs** (C4) | 2 stage files | MEDIUM — prose changes | Ready to ship |
| **Headless improvements** (U2 partial) | `headless_decisions[]` schema add, `--dry-run`, `--detect-only` flags | MEDIUM — needs contract design | Ready to ship |
| **Concurrency lock** (U3) | New behavior | MEDIUM — design decision (file lock? PID file?) | Ready to ship with simple file lock |
| **`[agent.gate_defaults]`** (C5) | New customize.toml schema | MEDIUM — depends on S1 | Ready to ship |
| **"Brief from preset" entry** (B2) | New interactive feature | **LOW — speculative product design** | ⚠️ Defer |
| **"Preview create-skill output" hop** (B3) | New stage between confirm and write | **LOW — speculative product design** | ⚠️ Defer |
| **UX polish in create-skill** (C6) | Rename-orphans cleanup, version-overwrite diff, Quick-tier upgrade hint | LOW–MEDIUM — partly speculative | ⚠️ Partial defer |
| **`skf-count-sentences.py`** (B5) | ~150 tok/run | LOW — marginal | ⚠️ Defer |
| **Customization scalar lifts in brief-skill** (B1) | 3 path scalars | HIGH | Ready to ship |
| **Workspace-list pagination spec** (B4) | Stage clarification | LOW — needs design | ⚠️ Defer or just remove the option |
| **Promote cancel-line** (B6) | One-line move | TRIVIAL | Ready to ship |

**The 4 items in the ⚠️ row are genuine product-design decisions** — building them blind risks hallucinating behavior the skill wasn't designed to have. The "DO NO HALLUCINATE" instruction tells me to flag these for design conversation rather than building speculatively.

**Recommended cut for this PR:** ship all green-row items (~25 of the 30). Defer the 5 speculative items to a follow-up issue with proper design.

This is still ~8 hours of focused work — substantial for one PR but achievable. After this confirmation I'll execute Phase A2 (build the 9 scripts) on the main thread, then fan out 3 parallel subagents for Phase B (per-skill elevation).

Acquire the lock before the workspace-hit check, hold it across fetch + checkout + rev-parse, AND keep holding it through the extraction-time read of the working tree. Two concurrent batch runs that target the same workspace clone but different `source_ref` values would otherwise race — one would `checkout` while the other was reading files mid-extraction, corrupting the inventory. The lock makes the per-workspace-repo unit of work serial. Use `flock -x {lockfile} -c "..."` or `fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX)`. If `flock` is unavailable, log a warning ("Concurrency guard unavailable — concurrent forges against the same workspace repo may produce inconsistent extraction inventories") and proceed.

10	Surgically updates existing skills when source code changes, preserving all [MANUAL] developer content while re-extracting only affected exports with full provenance tracking. Only changed exports are re-extracted — unchanged content is never touched. Every regenerated instruction must trace to code with file:line citations. Stack skills (`skill_type: "stack"` in metadata.json) are not supported by surgical update — use `skf-create-stack-skill` to re-compose from updated constituents. If a stack skill is provided, this workflow exits with a redirect message.
11	
12	## Conventions
13	
14	- Bare paths (e.g. `references/<name>.md`) resolve from the skill root.
15	- `references/` holds prompt content carved out of SKILL.md (workflow stages chained via frontmatter `nextStepFile`, plus static reference docs); `scripts/` and `assets/` hold deterministic helpers and templates.
16	- `{skill-root}` resolves to this skill's installed directory (where `customize.toml` lives, if present).
17	- `{project-root}`-prefixed paths resolve from the project working directory.
18	- `{skill-name}` resolves to the skill directory's basename.
19	
20	## Role
21	
22	You are a precision code analyst operating in Ferris Surgeon mode. This is a surgical operation, not an exploratory session. You bring AST-backed structural analysis and provenance-driven change detection expertise, while the source code provides the ground truth.
23	
24	## Workflow Rules
25	
26	These rules apply to every step in this workflow:
27	
28	- Never hallucinate — every statement must have AST provenance

{
  "command": "gh issue create --title \"Elevate skf-core skills — PR #2: shared scripts + headless improvements + §2a carve\" --body \"$(cat <<'EOF'\n## Background\n\nPR #306 shipped the **mechanical/parity** elevation work for the three remaining Core workflow skills (customize.toml × 3, language headers × 27, U4 conventions doc, B6 cancel-line). This issue tracks the **deferred substantial work** identified in the same quality-analysis pass that informed PR #306.\n\nSource quality-analysis reports (local, gitignored):\n- `skills/reports/skf-brief-skill/quality-analysis/20260515T115954/quality-report.md` (graded Excellent)\n- `skills/reports/skf-create-skill/quality-analysis/20260515T120003/quality-report.md` (graded Good — primary lift target)\n- `skills/reports/skf-update-skill/quality-analysis/20260515T120017/quality-report.md` (graded Excellent)\n\n## Workstream A — 9 shared script extractions\n\nEach extraction follows the pattern established by `skf-detect-tools.py` / `skf-merge-ccc-exclusions.py` in PR #305 (`49937672`): PEP 723 inline metadata, JSON I/O contract, paired test in `test/test-skf-*.py`, `uv run` invocation from stage prompts.\n\n### A1. `skf-description-guard.py` (S3 — cross-skill, highest value)\n\nCurrently duplicated as ~30 lines of identical 4-phase protocol prose in:\n- `src/skf-create-skill/references/validate.md` §0 \"Description Guard Protocol\" (line 31) and §8 \"Description Guard\" evidence-report block (line 232)\n- `src/skf-update-skill/references/write.md` §0 \"Description Guard Protocol\" (line 22) and §7 evidence-report block (line 151)\n\n**Proposed subcommands:**\n- `capture <skill-md>` → emits `{ guarded_description, schema_hash }` JSON; LLM stashes in context before any SKILL.md-modifying tool call\n- `verify-restore <skill-md> --captured <description>` → re-reads on-disk, compares, restores if divergent, emits `{ restored: bool, tool: str?, diff: str? }`\n\n**Companion file:** `src/shared/references/description-guard-protocol.md` — single source of truth for the 4-phase prose; both skills' stage files load it via frontmatter and stop restating the protocol inline.\n\n### A2–A6. update-skill deterministic ops (U1)\n\nPer quality-report A1 \"Lift Deterministic Operations into Scripts\" (HIGH):\n\n| Script | Extract from | Subcommand sketch |\n|---|---|---|\n| `skf-build-change-manifest.py` | `skf-update-skill/references/detect-changes.md` §3 | inputs: provenance map + current source tree → emits change manifest JSON |\n| `skf-provenance-gap-dispatch.py` | `references/detect-changes.md` (§1c gap-driven dispatcher) | reads drift report + brief scope → emits add/keep/drop classifications |\n| `skf-hash-content.py` | scattered SHA-256 prose | `hash <path>` → emits sha256 hex |\n| `skf-check-workspace-drift.py` | `references/remote-source-resolution.md` (git guard) | wraps `git status --porcelain` checks, emits clean/dirty enum |\n| `skf-update-active-symlink.py` | `references/write.md` (atomic symlink update) | atomic relink via temp + rename; emits before/after target |\n\n### A7–A9. create-skill deterministic ops (C2)\n\nPer quality-report C2 \"Script delegation for deterministic ops\" (HIGH):\n\n| Script | Extract from | Subcommand sketch |\n|---|---|---|\n| `skf-detect-scripts-assets.py` | `skf-create-skill/references/extract.md` §4c | walks source tree → classifies scripts vs assets per skill-sections.md rules |\n| `skf-resolve-authoritative-files.py` | `references/extract.md` §2a (authoritative-files protocol, ~95 lines) | resolves brief `scope.include` + canonical-doc heuristics → ranked file list |\n| `skf-validate-brief-schema.py` | `references/load-brief.md` §3 | validates loaded brief against `src/shared/scripts/schemas/skill-brief.v1.json` (already exists — script just wraps `jsonschema` invocation with skill-friendly error formatting) |\n\n## Workstream B — structural changes in create-skill\n\n### B1. Carve `extract.md` §2a to its own file (C3, medium)\n\n`src/skf-create-skill/references/extract.md` is 379 lines. §2a \"Authoritative Files Protocol\" embedded inside it accounts for ~95 lines. Carve to `references/authoritative-files-protocol.md` and load via frontmatter. Same pattern applies to `extraction-patterns.md` (430 lines) and `skill-sections.md` (395 lines) if appetite.\n\n### B2. Parallelize gh fetches (C4, medium — 5–18s wall-clock)\n\n- `references/sub/fetch-temporal.md` §3 — runs 4 independent `gh` fetches sequentially. Convert to `xargs -P 4` or background+wait pattern.\n- `references/sub/fetch-docs.md` §3 — runs up to 10 subpage fetches sequentially. Same pattern.\n\n## Workstream C — headless improvements in update-skill (U2, U3)\n\n### C1. `headless_decisions[]` in result contract (U2)\n\nCurrently auto-resolutions are logged inline as evidence-report lines but not surfaced as a structured field. Add a top-level `headless_decisions[]` array to `src/shared/scripts/schemas/skf-update-result-envelope.v1.json` (file may not yet exist — model on `skf-setup-result-envelope.v1.json`); each entry is `{ gate, default_action, taken_action, reason }`.\n\n### C2. `--dry-run` and `--detect-only` flags (U2)\n\n- `--dry-run`: run detect-changes + plan, emit envelope, skip write/merge\n- `--detect-only`: run detect-changes only, emit change manifest, exit\n\nMirror the CLI-knob pattern from skf-setup (`--orphan-action`, `--ccc-skip-index`, `--quiet` — see commit `3dd864cd`).\n\n### C3. Concurrency lock (U3)\n\nTwo simultaneous update-skill runs against the same `{forge_data_folder}/{skill_name}/` can corrupt provenance. Implement via `flock` on a lock file at `{forge_data_folder}/{skill_name}/.skf-update.lock`. Pattern already in use in `skf-create-skill/references/source-resolution-protocols.md:87` (workspace concurrency guard) — mirror it. Acquire on entry, release on exit. Now wire them in `src/skf-brief-skill/SKILL.md` activation so non-empty scalars override the bundled defaults. 28	
29	## MANDATORY SEQUENCE
30	
31	**CRITICAL:** Follow this sequence exactly. Do not skip, reorder, or improvise.
32	
33	### 0. Description Guard Protocol
34	
35	**Used by:** §2 (`skill-check check --fix`), §4 (`split-body`), and any future tool invocation that may modify SKILL.md.
36	
37	External validators occasionally rewrite the frontmatter `description` field — `skill-check --fix` may replace it with a generic or truncated version, and `split-body` may touch it during mechanical restructuring. The step 5 §2a compiled description is **authoritative**: it has already been sanitized of angle-bracket tokens and trigger-optimized for agent discovery. Losing it to a tool's well-meaning rewrite breaks discovery quality and re-introduces the angle-bracket failure mode.
38	
39	To prevent this, any tool invocation that may touch SKILL.md must run inside the following four-phase guard:
40	
41	1. **Capture.** Before invoking the tool, read the current SKILL.md frontmatter and snapshot the exact `description` value into a local variable (e.g., `guarded_description`). Capture the in-context copy as well.
42	2. **Execute.** Run the tool as specified in its section.
43	3. **Verify.** After the tool completes, re-read the on-disk SKILL.md and compare its frontmatter `description` against `guarded_description` as **token streams**: split each string on whitespace (`str.split()` — any run of spaces/tabs/newlines collapses) and compare the resulting lists element-by-element. This catches content divergence (missing words, replaced phrases, truncation, angle-bracket re-introduction) while ignoring cosmetic whitespace changes that a tool may apply (trailing newline, re-wrapped quoted strings). Do NOT use a normalized-string equality — a tool that rewrites `"foo  bar"` to `"foo bar"` (collapsed inner run) would trip a naive normalization even though no semantic content changed, and a tool that swapped one word would slip past a looser fuzzy match. Token-stream comparison is the sweet spot.
44	4. **Restore on divergence.** If the post-tool description differs from `guarded_description` in any way other than whitespace normalization, write `guarded_description` back to the on-disk SKILL.md frontmatter and update the in-context copy to match. Record `description_guard_restored: true` with the tool name in context for the evidence report.
45	5. **Re-validate restored description.** After a restore, run `uv run {project-root}/src/shared/scripts/skf-validate-frontmatter.py <staging-skill-dir>/SKILL.md` against the on-disk file to confirm the restored description still satisfies the frontmatter contract (length limits, forbidden tokens, required fields). The script declares pyyaml in its PEP 723 inline metadata; `uv run` resolves it automatically (per `docs/getting-started.md`'s uv prereq), while bare `python3` would `ModuleNotFoundError` on a fresh interpreter. Capture `schema_revalidation_result` in context. If the validator exits non-zero OR reports failure for the `description` field: flip the Schema result back to `FAIL` in the evidence report (overriding any prior PASS/WARN from §2), record `description_guard_revalidation: FAIL` with the validator's diagnostic message, and continue — do not halt (step 9 health-check and result contract still need to run so the failure is surfaced through the normal artifact path).
46	
47	**What counts as divergence:**
48	
49	- The description was replaced (different content).
50	- The description was truncated (suffix missing).
51	- Angle-bracket tokens were re-introduced (should never happen after step 5 §2a, but protect anyway).
52	- The field was deleted entirely (extreme tool behavior).
53	
54	**What does NOT count as divergence:** whitespace-only differences (trailing newline, trimmed spaces) — treat as equivalent.
55	
56	**Why this is centralized:** previously, §2 and §4 each contained their own capture/verify/restore prose. Duplicated defensive code drifts: a fix in one section doesn't propagate to the other, and adding a new tool invocation in the future requires remembering to copy the pattern. Centralizing the protocol gives step 6 one place to update when external validator behavior changes.
57	
58	### 1. Check Tool Availability
59	
60	Run: `timeout 30s npx skill-check -h` — the short timeout protects against a cold `npx` download blocking the workflow indefinitely on a slow network.
61	
62	- If succeeds: Continue to automated validation (section 2)
63	- If fails or times out: Perform manual fallback (section 3); add note to evidence-report: "Spec validation performed manually — skill-check tool unavailable". Also set `metadata.validation_status: 'manual-only'` in `metadata.json` (write via `python3 {atomicWriteHelper} write --target <staging-skill-dir>/metadata.json`), and in the evidence-report's `Validation Results` section mark Security, Body, and Content Quality (tessl) rows explicitly as `skipped — skill-check unavailable`. Downstream consumers (pipeline, forger, test-skill) check `validation_status` to decide how much weight to put on the artifact; leaving it unset would make a manual-only run look equivalent to a fully automated PASS.
64	
65	**Important:** Do not assume availability — empirical check required.
66	
67	### 2. Validate & Auto-Fix (skill-check check --fix)
68	
69	Run the external skill-check tool against the compiled skill staging directory.
70	
71	**Flag probe (run once, cache the result for §4 and §5 re-invocations):**
72	
73	```bash
74	npx skill-check --help 2>/dev/null | grep -- --no-security-scan
75	```
76	
77	- If the probe matches `--no-security-scan`: set `{security_scan_flag} = "--no-security-scan"`.
78	- Else run a second probe — `npx skill-check --help 2>/dev/null | grep -- --skip-security` — and if it matches, set `{security_scan_flag} = "--skip-security"`.
79	- If neither flag exists: set `{security_scan_flag} = ""` (empty) AND set `{skill_check_flag_fallback} = true`. Skip §2 and §4 automated flows entirely — fall through to §3 manual frontmatter validation. Record in evidence-report: `skill_check_flag_probe: neither --no-security-scan nor --skip-security supported by installed skill-check; validation performed manually`.
80	
81	**If a security-scan-disable flag was resolved (probe succeeded):**
82	
83	```bash
84	npx skill-check check <staging-skill-dir> --fix --format json {security_scan_flag}
85	```
86	
87	This performs frontmatter validation, description quality checks, body limit enforcement, local link resolution, file formatting, auto-fix of deterministic issues, and quality scoring (0-100) across five weighted categories.
88	
89	**Parse the JSON output** for: `qualityScore` (0-100), `diagnostics[]` (remaining issues), `fixed[]` (auto-corrected issues).
90	
91	**Description Guard Protocol:** This invocation may modify SKILL.md (especially when `fixed[]` is non-empty). Wrap the `skill-check check --fix` call in the four-phase protocol defined in §0: capture `guarded_description` before the call, execute, verify against the post-tool description, and restore on divergence. If `fixed[]` is non-empty, also re-read the modified SKILL.md to sync the in-context copy before proceeding — this prevents silent divergence between the in-context and on-disk versions that step 7 will use for artifact generation.
92	
93	**Note:** `skill-check` may return non-zero exit code even when `errorCount` is 0. Always rely on parsed JSON, not the shell exit code.
94	
95	- **Score ≥ 70:** Record "Schema: PASS (score: {score}/100)" in evidence-report
96	- **Score < 70:** Log remaining diagnostics as warnings, record "Schema: WARN — score {score}/100, {count} remaining issues", proceed
97	- **Unfixable errors:** Record specific rule IDs and suggestions, proceed with warnings
98	
99	### 3. Validate Frontmatter (Fallback)
100	
101	**If skill-check was available:** Skip — already validated in step 2.
102	
103	**If skill-check NOT available (fallback):** Perform manual frontmatter compliance check:
104	
105	- [ ] Frontmatter present — file starts with `---` and has closing `---`
106	- [ ] `name` field — present, non-empty, lowercase alphanumeric + hyphens only, 1-64 chars
107	- [ ] `name` matches skill output directory name

69	  - `exports_internal`: count of all other non-underscore-prefixed exports

1	# /// script
2	# requires-python = ">=3.10"
3	# dependencies = []
4	# ///
5	"""SKF Atomic Write — Crash-safe artifact writing for skill workflows.
6	
7	Provides three CLI subcommands skills can invoke via bash to avoid
8	partial-write corruption and active-symlink races.
9	
10	Subcommands:
11	  write      Stage content into <target>.skf-tmp, fsync, then rename to <target>.
12	             Content comes from stdin. Creates parent dirs as needed.
13	
14	  stage-dir  Create <target>.skf-tmp/ as a staging directory (mkdir -p).
15	             Caller writes files into it, then calls commit-dir to atomically
16	             swap it into place as <target>/ (with prior target moved aside
17	             to <target>.skf-rollback-<pid> and removed on success).
18	
19	  commit-dir Atomically swap <target>.skf-tmp/ into <target>/. If <target>/
20	             exists, move it to <target>.skf-rollback-<pid> first; on failure,
21	             restore. Supports rollback via --rollback to undo the most recent
22	             commit by restoring the rollback dir if still present.
23	
24	  flip-link  Atomically update symlink <link> to point at <target> using
25	             the `ln -sfn tmp && mv -Tf tmp link` pattern (or equivalent via
26	             os.replace on the link path). Holds an flock on <link>.lock.
27	
28	Cross-platform: locking branches between fcntl (POSIX) and msvcrt
29	(Windows). Symlink semantics on Windows require dev mode or admin —
30	flip-link surfaces a clear error rather than silently falling back.
31	Native Windows is untested in CI; the supported path is WSL2.
32	
33	Exit codes:
34	  0 on success
35	  1 on user error (bad args, missing input)
36	  2 on operation failure (disk full, permission, race-detected)
37	
38	CLI examples:
39	  cat metadata.json | python3 skf-atomic-write.py write --target /path/to/metadata.json
40	  python3 skf-atomic-write.py stage-dir --target /path/to/1.0.0

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Tests for skf-validate-brief-inputs.py.

The validator is pure — it parses a dict and returns a result envelope.
Tests build payloads inline and call validate() directly.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import importlib.util
import json
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

SCRIPT_PATH = (
    Path(__file__).parent.parent
    / "src"
    / "shared"
    / "scripts"
    / "skf-validate-brief-inputs.py"
)

spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("skf_validate_brief_inputs", SCRIPT_PATH)
mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(mod)

# Required fields
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------


class TestRequiredFields:
    def test_both_required_present_minimal_valid(self):
        out = mod.validate({"target_repo": "https://github.com/foo/bar", "skill_name": "foo-bar"})
        assert out["valid"] is True
        assert out["errors"] == []

  "content": "# /// script\n# requires-python = \">=3.10\"\n# dependencies = [\"pyyaml\"]\n# ///\n\"\"\"SKF Description Guard — defend SKILL.md frontmatter description against\nwell-meaning tool rewrites.\n\nExternal validators (`skill-check check --fix`, `skill-check split-body`) may\nrewrite the frontmatter `description` field — replace it with a generic\nversion, truncate it, or re-introduce angle-bracket tokens that earlier\nsanitization removed. The compiled/merged description on disk is the\nauthoritative one; losing it breaks agent discovery quality.\n\nThis script implements the deterministic parts of the four-phase guard\nprotocol (capture before tool call; verify-and-restore after) so that\nworkflows do not have to re-implement frontmatter parsing or token-stream\ncomparison in prose.\n\nSubcommands:\n  capture <skill-md>\n      Snapshot the current `description` field. Emits JSON\n      {\"description\": \"...\", \"schema_hash\": \"sha256:...\"}\n      where schema_hash covers the full frontmatter block (handy for\n      tamper detection if the caller wants belt-and-braces verification).\n\n  verify-restore <skill-md> --captured-description <STR>\n      Re-read the file, compare current description against the captured\n      value using token-stream equality (split on whitespace, compare\n      element-by-element). If diverged, atomically rewrite the frontmatter\n      with the captured description and emit\n        {\"diverged\": true, \"restored\": true|false, \"diff_kind\": \"...\",\n         \"current_description\": \"...\"}\n      If not diverged (including whitespace-only differences), emit\n        {\"diverged\": false, \"restored\": false, \"diff_kind\": \"none\"|\"whitespace-only\"}\n\nToken-stream comparison is the documented sweet spot — catches replaced\nwords, truncation, and reintroduced angle-brackets while ignoring cosmetic\nwhitespace fixes (trailing newline, re-wrapped quoted strings). See\nsrc/shared/references/description-guard-protocol.md for the full protocol.\n\nCLI — invoke via `uv run` so the PEP 723 PyYAML dependency declared above\nis auto-resolved:\n\n  uv run skf-description-guard.py capture <skill-md>\n  uv run skf-description-guard.py verify-restore <skill-md> \\\\\n      --captured-description \"the snapshot string\"\n\nExit codes:\n  0  — operation succeeded (including no-divergence verify)\n  1  — user error (bad args, file missing, frontmatter unparseable)\n  2  — operation failure (restore write failed)\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport hashlib\nimport json\nimport os\nimport sys\nimport tempfile\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport yaml\n\n\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Frontmatter parsing\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef _split_frontmatter(text: str) -> tuple[str, str, str]:\n    \"\"\"Split a markdown file into (leading, frontmatter_yaml, body).\n\n    Returns ('', '', text) if there is no frontmatter. Frontmatter is\n    recognized when the file starts with '---\\\\n' and a matching '---\\\\n'\n    line closes it before the body.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not text.startswith(\"---\\n\"):\n        return \"\", \"\", text\n    rest = text[4:]\n    close = rest.find(\"\\n---\\n\")\n    if close == -1:\n        # also accept '\\n---' as the closing line at EOF (no trailing newline)\n        if rest.endswith(\"\\n---\"):\n            return \"---\\n\", rest[: -len(\"\\n---\")], \"\"\n        return \"\", \"\", text\n    fm = rest[:close]\n    body = rest[close + len(\"\\n---\\n\") :]\n    return \"---\\n\", fm, body\n\n\ndef read_description(skill_md: Path) -> tuple[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"Read `description` field from SKILL.md frontmatter.\n\n    Returns (description, schema_hash). schema_hash is the sha256 of the\n    raw frontmatter YAML block as bytes, prefixed with \"sha256:\".\n\n    Raises ValueError if the file has no frontmatter, the frontmatter is\n    unparseable, or the description field is missing.\n    \"\"\"\n    text = skill_md.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    _, fm_yaml, _ = _split_frontmatter(text)\n    if not fm_yaml:\n        raise ValueError(f\"no frontmatter found in {skill_md}\")\n    try:\n        fm = yaml.safe_load(fm_yaml)\n    except yaml.YAMLError as exc:\n        raise ValueError(f\"frontmatter in {skill_md} is not valid YAML: {exc}\") from exc\n    if not isinstance(fm, dict):\n        raise ValueError(f\"frontmatter in {skill_md} is not a mapping\")\n    if \"description\" not in fm:\n        raise ValueError(f\"frontmatter in {skill_md} has no `description` field\")\n    description = fm[\"description\"]\n    if not isinstance(description, str):\n        raise ValueError(f\"`description` in {skill_md} is not a string\")\n    schema_hash = \"sha256:\" + hashlib.sha256(fm_yaml.encode(\"utf-8\")).hexdigest()\n    return description, schema_hash\n\n\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Divergence detection\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef classify_divergence(captured: str, current: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Compare two descriptions and classify the difference.\n\n    Returns one of:\n      \"none\"            — strings are byte-identical\n      \"whitespace-only\" — token streams match but raw strings differ\n      \"replaced\"        — token streams differ (semantic content change)\n      \"truncated\"       — current's tokens are a strict prefix of captured's\n      \"deleted\"         — current is empty/whitespace-only and captured is not\n    \"\"\"\n    if captured == current:\n        return \"none\"\n    if not current.strip() and captured.strip():\n        return \"deleted\"\n    cap_tokens = captured.split()\n    cur_tokens = current.split()\n    if cap_tokens == cur_tokens:\n        return \"whitespace-only\"\n    # truncation = cur_tokens is a strict prefix of cap_tokens\n    if len(cur_tokens) < len(cap_tokens) and cap_tokens[: len(cur_tokens)] == cur_tokens:\n        return \"truncated\"\n    return \"replaced\"\n\n\ndef is_diverged(diff_kind: str) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Whether a diff_kind indicates real (non-whitespace) divergence.\"\"\"\n    return diff_kind not in (\"none\", \"whitespace-only\")\n\n\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Restore (atomic frontmatter rewrite)\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef restore_description(skill_md: Path, captured: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Atomically rewrite SKILL.md so its frontmatter `description` equals captured.\n\n    Preserves frontmatter key order and surrounding whitespace by doing a\n    line-level rewrite of just the `description:` value, not a full YAML\n    re-dump (which would re-order keys, change quoting style, and likely\n    fail roundtrip tests downstream).\n    \"\"\"\n    text = skill_md.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    leading, fm_yaml, body = _split_frontmatter(text)\n    if not fm_yaml:\n        raise ValueError(f\"cannot restore: no frontmatter in {skill_md}\")\n\n    new_fm = _rewrite_description_line(fm_yaml, captured)\n    new_text = f\"{leading}{new_fm}\\n---\\n{body}\"\n\n    # atomic: write to a sibling temp file, fsync, rename\n    fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(\n        prefix=skill_md.name + \".\", suffix=\".skf-guard.tmp\", dir=skill_md.parent\n    )\n    try:\n        with os.fdopen(fd, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as tmp:\n            tmp.write(new_text)\n            tmp.flush()\n            os.fsync(tmp.fileno())\n        os.replace(tmp_path, skill_md)\n    except Exception:\n        try:\n            os.unlink(tmp_path)\n        except FileNotFoundError:\n            pass\n        raise\n\n\ndef _rewrite_description_line(fm_yaml: str, new_description: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Replace the `description:` value in a YAML frontmatter block.\n\n    Preserves other keys verbatim. Handles three common shapes:\n      description: single-line value\n      description: \"double-quoted value\"\n      description: |     # block scalar (folded variant: >)\n        multi-line\n        value here\n    \"\"\"\n    lines = fm_yaml.split(\"\\n\")\n    out: list[str] = []\n    i = 0\n    quoted = _yaml_quote_inline(new_description)\n    replaced = False\n    while i < len(lines):\n        line = lines[i]\n        if not replaced and _is_description_key_line(line):\n            stripped = line.lstrip()\n            indent = line[: len(line) - len(stripped)]\n            # detect block-scalar indicator (| or >)\n            after_key = stripped[len(\"description:\") :].lstrip()\n            if after_key.startswith(\"|\") or after_key.startswith(\">\"):\n                # skip block-scalar continuation lines (deeper indent than the key line)\n                key_indent = len(indent)\n                i += 1\n                while i < len(lines):\n                    nxt = lines[i]\n                    if nxt.strip() == \"\":\n                        # blank lines belong to the block scalar\n                        i += 1\n                        continue\n                    nxt_indent = len(nxt) - len(nxt.lstrip())\n                    if nxt_indent <= key_indent:\n                        break\n                    i += 1\n                out.append(f\"{indent}description: {quoted}\")\n                replaced = True\n                continue\n            out.append(f\"{indent}description: {quoted}\")\n            replaced = True\n            i += 1\n            continue\n        out.append(line)\n        i += 1\n    if not replaced:\n        raise ValueError(\"description key not found while rewriting frontmatter\")\n    return \"\\n\".join(out)\n\n\ndef _is_description_key_line(line: str) -> bool:\n    stripped = line.lstrip()\n    return stripped.startswith(\"description:\") and (\n        len(stripped) == len(\"description:\") or stripped[len(\"description:\")] in (\" \", \"\\t\", \"\")\n    )\n\n\ndef _yaml_quote_inline(value: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Emit a YAML scalar suitable as the inline value of `description: `.\n\n    Uses double-quoted form so control characters and embedded quotes are\n    safe. Block scalars (| / >) are not used — the description field is a\n    single semantic string and downstream readers (skill-check, agentskills)\n    expect inline form.\n    \"\"\"\n    escaped = (\n        value.replace(\"\\\\\", \"\\\\\\\\\")\n        .replace(\"\\\"\", \"\\\\\\\"\")\n        .replace(\"\\n\", \"\\\\n\")\n        .replace(\"\\r\", \"\\\\r\")\n        .replace(\"\\t\", \"\\\\t\")\n    )\n    return f'\"{escaped}\"'\n\n\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# CLI\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef _cmd_capture(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:\n    skill_md = Path(args.skill_md)\n    if not skill_md.is_file():\n        _fail(f\"file not found: {skill_md}\")\n    try:\n        description, schema_hash = read_description(skill_md)\n    except ValueError as exc:\n        _fail(str(exc))\n    json.dump({\"description\": description, \"schema_hash\": schema_hash}, sys.stdout)\n    sys.stdout.write(\"\\n\")\n    return 0\n\n\ndef _cmd_verify_restore(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:\n    skill_md = Path(args.skill_md)\n    if not skill_md.is_file():\n        _fail(f\"file not found: {skill_md}\")\n    try:\n        current, _ = read_description(skill_md)\n    except ValueError as exc:\n        _fail(str(exc))\n\n    captured = args.captured_description\n    diff_kind = classify_divergence(captured, current)\n    diverged = is_diverged(diff_kind)\n\n    result = {\n        \"diverged\": diverged,\n        \"restored\": False,\n        \"diff_kind\": diff_kind,\n        \"current_description\": current,\n    }\n\n    if diverged:\n        try:\n            restore_description(skill_md, captured)\n            result[\"restored\"] = True\n        except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:\n            json.dump({**result, \"restore_error\": str(exc)}, sys.stdout)\n            sys.stdout.write(\"\\n\")\n            return 2\n\n    json.dump(result, sys.stdout)\n    sys.stdout.write(\"\\n\")\n    return 0\n\n\ndef _fail(msg: str) -> None:\n    print(f\"error: {msg}\", file=sys.stderr)\n    raise SystemExit(1)\n\n\ndef _build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(\n        prog=\"skf-description-guard\",\n        description=\"Defend SKILL.md frontmatter description against tool rewrites.\",\n    )\n    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest=\"cmd\", required=True)\n\n    p_cap = sub.add_parser(\"capture\", help=\"snapshot the current description value\")\n    p_cap.add_argument(\"skill_md\", help=\"path to SKILL.md\")\n    p_cap.set_defaults(func=_cmd_capture)\n\n    p_ver = sub.add_parser(\n        \"verify-restore\",\n        help=\"verify on-disk description against captured snapshot; restore if diverged\",\n    )\n    p_ver.add_argument(\"skill_md\", help=\"path to SKILL.md\")\n    p_ver.add_argument(\n        \"--captured-description\",\n        required=True,\n        help=\"the description string captured before the tool call\",\n    )\n    p_ver.set_defaults(func=_cmd_verify_restore)\n\n    return parser\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    parser = _build_parser()\n    args = parser.parse_args(argv)\n    return args.func(args)\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    raise SystemExit(main())\n"

1	# Headless Gate Convention
2	
3	## Overview
4	
5	Gates are user interaction points where a workflow pauses for confirmation or input. In headless mode, gates auto-resolve with their default action. This convention ensures one code path with two behaviors — interactive and headless use the same gates, the same output, and the same progression logic.
6	
7	## How It Works
8	
9	Every gate in a step file follows this pattern:
10	
11	```
12	**GATE: [default action]** — Present [options] to user.
13	If `{headless_mode}`: auto-proceed with [default action], log: "headless: auto-[action]".
14	```
15	
16	The gate always:
17	1. Prepares the same output (summary, preview, menu) regardless of mode
18	2. In interactive mode: displays the output and waits for user input
19	3. In headless mode: displays the output, logs the auto-action, and proceeds with the default
20	
21	## Resolving `{headless_mode}`
22	
23	`{headless_mode}` is resolved during activation from:
24	1. **Args:** `--headless` or `-H` passed to the skill invocation
25	2. **Preferences:** `headless_mode: true` in `{sidecar_path}/preferences.yaml`
```

{
  "file_path": "/home/armel/Projects/OSS/bmad-module-skill-forge/src/shared/references/description-guard-protocol.md",
  "content": "# Description Guard Protocol\n\n## Overview\n\nExternal validators (`skill-check check --fix`, `skill-check split-body`, and any future tool that may rewrite SKILL.md frontmatter) occasionally replace, truncate, or otherwise mutate the `description` field — sometimes substituting a generic version, sometimes re-introducing angle-bracket tokens that earlier sanitization removed.\n\nThe on-disk description is **authoritative**: it has been compiled (in `skf-create-skill`) or merged (in `skf-update-skill`) with deliberate trigger-optimization. Losing it to a tool's well-meaning rewrite breaks agent discovery quality and can re-introduce the angle-bracket failure mode that breaks tessl on the next run.\n\nAny tool invocation that may touch SKILL.md must run inside the four-phase guard below. Workflows invoke the deterministic phases (1, 3, 4) via `src/shared/scripts/skf-description-guard.py`; the LLM only performs phase 2 (the tool call itself).\n\n## The Four-Phase Guard\n\n### 1. Capture\n\nBefore invoking the tool, snapshot the on-disk `description` value:\n\n```bash\nuv run {project-root}/src/shared/scripts/skf-description-guard.py \\\n    capture <skill-md-path>\n```\n\nOutput JSON:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"description\": \"the snapshotted value\",\n  \"schema_hash\": \"sha256:...\"\n}\n```\n\nStash the `description` value in workflow context as `guarded_description`. Also keep the in-context copy synced with the on-disk pre-call state.\n\n### 2. Execute\n\nRun the tool as specified in its section. The LLM performs this step normally — `skill-check check --fix`, `skill-check split-body`, or whatever is documented in the calling stage.\n\n### 3 + 4. Verify and Restore\n\nAfter the tool completes, run:\n\n```bash\nuv run {project-root}/src/shared/scripts/skf-description-guard.py \\\n    verify-restore <skill-md-path> \\\n    --captured-description \"{guarded_description}\"\n```\n\nThe script:\n\n1. Re-reads on-disk `description`\n2. Compares against `guarded_description` using **token-stream equality** — split each string on whitespace, compare resulting token lists element-by-element\n3. If diverged: atomically rewrites the frontmatter `description` field with `guarded_description`\n\nOutput JSON:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"diverged\": true|false,\n  \"restored\": true|false,\n  \"diff_kind\": \"none|whitespace-only|replaced|truncated|deleted\",\n  \"current_description\": \"what was on disk before any restore\"\n}\n```\n\nIf `restored == true`, also update the in-context copy of `description` to match `guarded_description` so subsequent stages do not work from a stale tool-mutated version. Record `description_guard_restored: true` (with the tool name) in workflow context for the evidence report.\n\n## Why Token-Stream Comparison\n\nToken-stream comparison is the documented sweet spot between two failure modes:\n\n- **Looser fuzzy matching** would let a tool swap one word past the guard (e.g., replace \"compile\" with \"build\").\n- **Naive whitespace-normalized equality** would trip on a tool that collapses `\"foo  bar\"` → `\"foo bar\"` (cosmetic whitespace fix), forcing unnecessary restore writes.\n\nSplitting on whitespace and comparing token lists catches replaced words, truncation, deletion, and angle-bracket re-introduction while ignoring trailing newlines, re-wrapped quoted strings, and collapsed inner runs.\n\n## What Counts as Divergence\n\n- **`replaced`** — different content (any word changed)\n- **`truncated`** — current tokens are a strict prefix of captured\n- **`deleted`** — the field is empty or whitespace-only on disk\n- **`whitespace-only`** — token streams match but raw strings differ (**not** divergence; do not restore)\n- **`none`** — byte-identical (**not** divergence)\n\n## Post-Restore Re-Validation (Optional)\n\nSkills that run frontmatter compliance checks (e.g. `skf-create-skill validate.md`) should additionally re-validate the restored description against the frontmatter contract after restore — a restored value must still satisfy length limits, forbidden-token rules, and required-field shape. Run:\n\n```bash\nuv run {project-root}/src/shared/scripts/skf-validate-frontmatter.py <skill-md-path>\n```\n\nIf the validator reports failure for the `description` field, flip the Schema row in the evidence report back to `FAIL` and record `description_guard_revalidation: FAIL` with the validator diagnostic. Do not halt — let the failure surface through the normal artifact path so step health-check and the result contract record it.\n\n## Why This Protocol Is Centralized\n\nPreviously, each tool invocation in each calling stage carried its own copy of the capture/verify/restore prose. Duplicated defensive logic drifts: a fix in one section did not propagate to the other, and adding a new tool invocation required remembering to copy the pattern. Centralizing the protocol gives every calling stage one place to update when external validator behavior changes.\n\n## Calling Workflows\n\n- `src/skf-create-skill/references/validate.md` — wraps `skill-check check --fix` (§2) and `split-body` (§4). Runs the optional post-restore re-validation.\n- `src/skf-update-skill/references/write.md` — wraps `skill-check check --fix` and `skill-check split-body --write` in §7. Does not run post-restore re-validation today; the post-write checks in §1 catch downstream issues.\n"
}

126	**Mandatory approach — selective split:** Identify Tier 2 sections by their `## Full` heading prefix (e.g., `## Full API Reference`, `## Full Type Definitions`, `## Full Integration Patterns`). Extract ONLY those sections to `references/`, starting with the largest. Keep ALL Tier 1 content and any smaller sections inline. 128	**FORBIDDEN:** Running `npx skill-check split-body --write` without prior selective extraction. This command is a LAST RESORT only after selective split has been attempted and proven insufficient.
129	
130	**If selective split alone does not bring body under the limit** (rare — typically only occurs when Tier 1 itself exceeds 300 lines): reduce Tier 1 Key API Summary and Architecture at a Glance sections to fit within limits. Do NOT fall back to automated `split-body --write` to solve a Tier 1 sizing problem.
131	
132	**Tier 1 preservation check:** After ANY split operation, verify that ALL of the following sections remain inline in SKILL.md (not moved to references/): Overview, Quick Start, Common Workflows, Key API Summary, Migration & Deprecation Warnings (if present), Key Types, Architecture at a Glance, CLI (if present), Scripts & Assets (if present), Manual Sections. If any Tier 1 section was moved to references/, restore it immediately and re-split targeting only Tier 2 sections.
133	
134	**Post-split Tier-1 count check (mandatory):** before invoking the splitter, count the Tier-1 `##`-level section headings present in SKILL.md (any heading whose title matches one of the Tier-1 names listed above) and store as `tier1_count_pre`. After the split completes, recount as `tier1_count_post`. **HALT** if `tier1_count_post < tier1_count_pre` with: "Split reduced Tier-1 section count from {pre} to {post}. Tier-1 sections must remain inline. Restoring from staging backup and aborting body split — manual review required." Do not proceed past §4 — Tier-1 preservation is a hard invariant and a count drop indicates the splitter pulled an inline section into references/ regardless of the section-list check above (e.g., heading-text variation, capitalization, or the splitter's own heuristics).
135	
136	**Anchor validation and remediation:** After any split, verify that context-snippet section anchors (`#quick-start`, `#key-types`) still resolve to headings in SKILL.md. 49	## Script/Asset Extraction Patterns
50	
51	Scripts and assets are file-level artifacts, not code exports. They follow the **file-copy extraction method** — detected in source, copied with provenance citations.
52	
53	### Detection Heuristics
54	
55	**Script directories:** `scripts/`, `bin/`, `tools/`, `cli/`
56	**Asset directories:** `assets/`, `templates/`, `schemas/`, `configs/`, `examples/`
57	
58	**Script file signals:**
59	
60	| Signal                  | Strength | Pattern                                                                              |
61	|-------------------------|----------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
62	| Entry point declaration | Strong   | `package.json` `bin` field, Cargo.toml `[[bin]]`, pyproject.toml `[project.scripts]` |
63	| Shebang + executable    | Strong   | `#!/bin/bash`, `#!/usr/bin/env python`, `#!/usr/bin/env node`                        |
64	| CLI argument parser     | Moderate | `argparse`, `yargs`, `commander`, `cobra`, `clap` imports in file                    |
65	| Directory convention    | Moderate | File in `scripts/`, `bin/`, `tools/` directory                                       |
66	| CI/CD reference         | Moderate | Script referenced in `.github/workflows/*.yml`                                       |
67	
68	**Asset file signals:**
69	
70	| Signal           | Strength | Pattern                                             |
71	|------------------|----------|-----------------------------------------------------|
72	| JSON Schema      | Strong   | `*.schema.json`, file contains `"$schema"` key      |
73	| Config template  | Strong   | `*.example`, `*.template.*`, `*.sample` extension   |
74	| Official example | Moderate | File in `examples/` directory, referenced in README |
75	| OpenAPI/GraphQL  | Moderate | `openapi.json`, `*.graphql`, `swagger.yaml`         |
76	| Design tokens    | Weak     | `tokens.json`, `theme.json` in `assets/`            |
77	
78	### Inclusion Rules
79	
80	- Only include files within brief's `scope.include` patterns (or auto-detected directories)
81	- Exclude binary files (check extension: `.so`, `.dll`, `.jar`, `.wasm`, `.exe`)
82	- Exclude generated files (`dist/`, `build/`, `.webpack/` output)
83	- Exclude vendored/third-party files
84	- Flag files >500 lines for user confirmation (may be too large for skill package)
85	- If `scripts_intent` is absent from the brief, treat as `"detect"` (auto-detection is the default). If `scripts_intent` is explicitly `"none"`, skip scripts detection. Same rule applies to `assets_intent`.
86	
87	### Provenance and Hashing
88	
89	Each extracted file receives:
90	- Citation: `[SRC:{source_path}:L1]` (T1-low — file verified to exist but content not AST-analyzed)
91	- Content hash: SHA-256 of file content (for drift detection in audit-skill)
92	- Extraction method: `"file-copy"` (distinct from `"ast_bridge"` for code exports)
93	
94	### Inventory Structure
95	
96	**Script inventory entry:**
97	- `name`: filename (e.g., `validate-config.sh`)
98	- `source_file`: path relative to source root
99	- `purpose`: extracted from file header comments or README reference (if none found, use filename)
100	- `language`: detected from extension or shebang
101	- `content_hash`: SHA-256
102	- `confidence`: T1-low
103	
104	**Asset inventory entry:**
105	- `name`: filename (e.g., `config-schema.json`)
106	- `source_file`: path relative to source root
107	- `purpose`: extracted from file header or schema `title`/`description` field
108	- `type`: `template`, `schema`, `config`, `example`
109	- `content_hash`: SHA-256
110	- `confidence`: T1-low
111	
```

return True, detect_shebang_language(path)\n    shebang_lang = detect_shebang_language(path)\n    if shebang_lang is not None:\n        return True, shebang_lang\n    return False, None\n\n\n# leading content.\n\n    Heuristics (first match wins):\n      - JSON schema: read top-level `title` or `description` field\n      - Files with header comments: first comment line after any shebang\n 1024)\n        if text:\n            try:\n                data = json.loads(text)\n                for key in (\"title\", \"description\"):\n                    val = data.get(key) if isinstance(data, dict) else None\n                    if isinstance(val, str) and val.strip():\n                        return val.strip()\n            except json.JSONDecodeError:\n                pass\n\n    text = read_text_safe(path, max_bytes=4 * 1024)\n    if text:\n        for i, line in enumerate(text.splitlines()[:10]):\n            if i == 0 and line.startswith(\"#!\"):\n match.group(1).strip().rstrip(\"*/\").strip()\n                if purpose:\n                    return purpose\n\n    return path.name\n\n\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Build records\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef build_script_record(\n    path: Path, source_root: Path, *, shebang_lang: str | None, max_lines: int\n) -> dict:\n    rel = str(path.relative_to(source_root))\n    lines = count_lines(path)\n    return {\n        \"name\": path.name,\n        \"source_file\": rel,\n        \"purpose\": extract_purpose(path, asset_type_hint=None),\n        \"language\": detect_language(path, shebang_lang=shebang_lang),\n        \"content_hash\": sha256_of_file(path),\n        \"confidence\": CONFIDENCE,\n        \"lines\": lines,\n        \"size_flag\": \"oversized\" if lines > max_lines else None,\n    }\n\n\ndef build_asset_record(\n    path: Path, source_root: Path, *, atype: str, max_lines: int\n) -> dict:\n    rel = str(path.relative_to(source_root))\n    lines = count_lines(path)\n    return {\n        \"name\": path.name,\n        \"source_file\": rel,\n        \"purpose\": extract_purpose(path, asset_type_hint=atype),\n        \"type\": atype,\n        \"content_hash\": sha256_of_file(path),\n        \"confidence\": CONFIDENCE,\n        \"lines\": lines,\n        \"size_flag\": \"oversized\" if lines > max_lines else None,\n    }\n\n\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Main detection\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef detect(\n    source_root: Path,\n    *,\n    scripts_intent: str = \"detect\",\n    assets_intent: str = \"detect\",\n    scope_patterns: list[str] | None = None,\n    max_lines: int = 500,\n) -> dict:\n    scope_patterns = scope_patterns or []\n    scripts_skipped = scripts_intent == \"none\"\n    assets_skipped = assets_intent == \"none\"\n\n    scripts_inventory: list[dict] = []\n    assets_inventory: list[dict] = []\n    files_scanned = 0\n\n    entry_points = (\n        entry_point_script_paths(source_root) if not scripts_skipped else set()\n    )\n\n    if not scripts_skipped or not assets_skipped:\n        for path in iter_files(source_root):\n            files_scanned += 1\n            if is_binary_path(path):\n                continue\n            if not matches_scope(path, source_root, scope_patterns):\n                continue\n\n            if not scripts_skipped:\n                is_scr, shebang_lang = is_script(\n                    path, source_root, entry_points=entry_points\n                )\n                if is_scr:\n                    scripts_inventory.append(\n                        build_script_record(\n                            path, source_root,\n                            shebang_lang=shebang_lang, max_lines=max_lines,\n                        )\n                    )\n                    continue  # a script can't also be an asset\n\n            if not assets_skipped:\n                atype = asset_type(path, source_root)\n                if atype is not None:\n                    assets_inventory.append(\n                        build_asset_record(\n                            path, source_root, atype=atype, max_lines=max_lines,\n                        )\n                    )\n\n    # Deterministic ordering for stable diffs / cacheability\n    scripts_inventory.sort(key=lambda r: r[\"source_file\"])\n    assets_inventory.sort(key=lambda r: r[\"source_file\"])\n\n    return {\n        \"scripts_inventory\": scripts_inventory,\n        \"assets_inventory\": assets_inventory,\n        \"scripts_skipped\": scripts_skipped,\n        \"assets_skipped\": assets_skipped,\n        \"stats\": {\n            \"scripts_found\": len(scripts_inventory),\n            \"assets_found\": len(assets_inventory),\n            \"files_scanned\": files_scanned,\n        },\n    }\n\n\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# CLI\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef _cmd_detect(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:\n    source_root = Path(args.source_root).resolve()\n    if not source_root.is_dir():\n        print(f\"error: source root not a directory: {source_root}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return 1\n    scope_patterns = (\n        [s.strip() for s in args.scope_include.split(\",\") if s.strip()]\n        if args.scope_include\n        else []\n    )\n    if args.scripts_intent not in (\"detect\", \"none\"):\n        print(f\"error: --scripts-intent must be detect|none\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return 1\n    if args.assets_intent not in (\"detect\", \"none\"):\n        print(f\"error: --assets-intent must be detect|none\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return 1\n\n    result = detect(\n        source_root,\n        scripts_intent=args.scripts_intent,\n        assets_intent=args.assets_intent,\n        scope_patterns=scope_patterns,\n        max_lines=args.max_lines,\n    )\n    json.dump(result, sys.stdout, indent=2)\n    sys.stdout.write(\"\\n\")\n    return 0\n\n\ndef _build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(\n        prog=\"skf-detect-scripts-assets\",\n        description=\"Detect script and asset files in a source tree per SKF extraction rules.\",\n    )\n    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest=\"cmd\", required=True)\n    p = sub.add_parser(\"detect\", help=\"scan a source tree and emit inventory JSON\")\n    p.add_argument(\"source_root\", help=\"path to the source tree root\")\n    p.add_argument(\n        \"--scripts-intent\",\n        default=\"detect\",\n        help=\"detect|none (default: detect)\",\n    )\n    p.add_argument(\n        \"--assets-intent\",\n        default=\"detect\",\n        help=\"detect|none (default: detect)\",\n    )\n    p.add_argument(\n        \"--scope-include\",\n        default=None,\n        help=\"comma-separated glob patterns to limit detection (relative to source-root)\",\n    )\n    p.add_argument(\n        \"--max-lines\",\n        type=int,\n        default=500,\n        help=\"files above this line count get size_flag='oversized' (default: 500)\",\n    )\n    p.set_defaults(func=_cmd_detect)\n    return parser\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    parser = _build_parser()\n    args = parser.parse_args(argv)\n    return args.func(args)\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    raise SystemExit(main())\n"

Scan source tree for directories/files matching detection heuristics (scripts/, bin/, tools/, cli/ for scripts; assets/, templates/, schemas/, configs/, examples/ for assets)\n2.   "new_string": "### 4c. Detect and Inventory Scripts/Assets\n\n**Default resolution:** If `scripts_intent` is absent from the brief, treat as `\"detect\"` (auto-detection). If `assets_intent` is absent, treat as `\"detect\"`. Only an explicit `\"none\"` value disables detection.\n\nInvoke the deterministic detector — it implements the heuristics from `{extractionPatternsTracingData}` (directory conventions, shebang signals, `package.json` `bin` entry-points, asset filename patterns, binary-extension exclusion, generated-path pruning) so this stage doesn't re-derive them per-run:\n\n```bash\nuv run {detectScriptsAssetsHelper} detect <source-root> \\\n    --scripts-intent <scripts_intent> \\\n    --assets-intent <assets_intent> \\\n    [--scope-include \"<glob1>,<glob2>,...\"] \\\n    [--max-lines 500]\n```\n\nThe helper emits JSON on stdout:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"scripts_inventory\": [ {name, source_file, purpose, language, content_hash, confidence, lines, size_flag}, ... ],\n  \"assets_inventory\":  [ {name, source_file, purpose, type,     content_hash, confidence, lines, size_flag}, ... ],\n  \"scripts_skipped\": <bool>,\n  \"assets_skipped\":  <bool>,\n  \"stats\": { \"scripts_found\": N, \"assets_found\": M, \"files_scanned\": K }\n}\n```\n\nMerge `scripts_inventory[]` and `assets_inventory[]` into the running extraction inventory verbatim — entries already carry `confidence: \"T1-low\"` and `content_hash` (sha256:...). Records with `size_flag: \"oversized\"` should be surfaced in §6 (Extraction Summary) so the user can confirm before bundling. If both `scripts_skipped` and `assets_skipped` are true, the helper performs no walk and §4c is effectively a no-op."

244	- Cross-reference deleted files/exports with added files/exports

Forge and above: use ast-grep to compare export signatures between the deleted and added files. Forge+/Deep: use CCC semantic similarity when available

  "content": "# /// script\n# requires-python = \">=3.10\"\n# dependencies = []\n# ///\n\"\"\"SKF Hash Content — SHA-256 hashing helpers for skill workflows.\n\nTwo patterns recur across the update-skill workflow's stage prose:\n\n  1. **Single-file hash** — detect-changes.md §1b, when a candidate file is\n     promoted into `brief.scope.include`, the LLM is asked to \"compute SHA-256\n     content hash of candidate.path\" and emit a record\n     `{path, heuristic, size_bytes, line_count, content_hash}` for\n     `promoted_docs_new[]`. Same hashing primitive,\n     iterated, plus a stat-and-compare. NEW_FILE detection is intentionally\n     out of scope here — that lives in `skf-detect-scripts-assets.py`.\n\nSubcommands:\n  hash <path> [--include-path]\n      Emit JSON {\"content_hash\": \"sha256:...\", \"size_bytes\": N, \"line_count\": L}\n      for a single file. With --include-path, the record also includes\n      \"path\": <as given>, so batch callers can collect records by streaming\n      multiple invocations.\n\n  compare <source-root> --provenance-map <path>\n      Read `file_entries[]` from a provenance-map JSON and classify each row\n      against the current source tree.
