Matches the convention used\nby skf-detect-scripts-assets.py and the existing prose (\"SHA-256 content\nhash\" — agnostic about prefix, but the prefix is the SKF convention to make\nhashes self-describing for future algorithm migrations).\n\nCLI examples:\n  uv run skf-hash-content.py hash docs/AGENTS.md\n  uv run skf-hash-content.py hash docs/AGENTS.md --include-path\n  uv run skf-hash-content.py compare /path/to/source \\\\\n      --provenance-map /path/to/provenance-map.json\n\nExit codes:\n  0  — operation succeeded (including: file in compare missing on disk;\n       its classification is DELETED_FILE, not an error)\n  1  — user error (bad path, malformed JSON, missing required field)\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport hashlib\nimport json\nimport sys\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\n\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Hashing primitives\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef sha256_of_file(path: Path) -> str:\n    \"\"\"SHA-256 of file content, with sha256: prefix.\"\"\"\n    h = hashlib.sha256()\n    with path.open(\"rb\") as fh:\n        for chunk in iter(lambda: fh.read(65536), b\"\"):\n            h.update(chunk)\n    return \"sha256:\" + h.hexdigest()\n\n\ndef count_lines(path: Path) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Count newlines in file content; 0 if unreadable.\"\"\"\n    n = 0\n    try:\n        with path.open(\"rb\") as fh:\n            for chunk in iter(lambda: fh.read(65536), b\"\"):\n                n += chunk.count(b\"\\n\")\n    except OSError:\n        return 0\n    return n\n\n\ndef hash_record(path: Path, *, include_path: bool = False) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Build a single-file record: content_hash + size_bytes + line_count.\"\"\"\n    rec: dict = {\n        \"content_hash\": sha256_of_file(path),\n        \"size_bytes\": path.stat().st_size,\n        \"line_count\": count_lines(path),\n    }\n    if include_path:\n        rec = {\"path\": str(path), **rec}\n    return rec\n\n\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Provenance comparison\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\nUNCHANGED = \"UNCHANGED\"\nMODIFIED_FILE = \"MODIFIED_FILE\"\nDELETED_FILE = \"DELETED_FILE\"\n\n\ndef load_file_entries(provenance_path: Path) -> list[dict]:\n    \"\"\"Extract the file_entries list from a provenance file.\n\n    Accepts two shapes:\n      - top-level object with a `file_entries` key (canonical)\n      - top-level array of entries (already-extracted)\n\n    Returns a copy of the list. Raises ValueError on malformed JSON or\n    missing key.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        data = json.loads(provenance_path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n    except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError) as raise ValueError(\n        f\"provenance file {provenance_path} must be an object or array; \"\n        f\"got {type(data).__name__}\"\n    )\n\n\ndef classify_entry(source_root: Path, entry: dict) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Classify a single file_entry against the current source tree.\"\"\"\n    source_file = entry.get(\"source_file\")\n    stored_hash = entry.get(\"content_hash\")\n    if not isinstance(source_file, str):\n        raise ValueError(f\"file_entry missing required `source_file`: {entry!r}\")\n\n    current = (source_root / source_file).resolve()\n    # guard against ../.. \"current_hash\": None,\n            \"current_size_bytes\": None,\n        }\n\n    current_hash = sha256_of_file(current)\n    if current_hash == stored_hash:\n        classification = UNCHANGED\n \"current_hash\": current_hash,\n        \"current_size_bytes\": current.stat().st_size,\n    }\n\n\ndef compare(source_root: Path, provenance_path: Path) -> dict:\n    entries = load_file_entries(provenance_path)\n    comparisons = [classify_entry(source_root, entry) for entry in entries]\n    counts = {UNCHANGED: 0, MODIFIED_FILE: 0, DELETED_FILE: 0}\n    for c in \"unchanged\": counts[UNCHANGED],\n            \"modified\": counts[MODIFIED_FILE],\n            \"deleted\": counts[DELETED_FILE],\n        },\n    }\n\n\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# CLI\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef _cmd_hash(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:\n    path = Path(args.path)\n    if not path.is_file():\n        print(f\"error: file not found: {path}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return 1\n    rec = hash_record(path, include_path=args.include_path)\n    json.dump(rec, sys.stdout)\n    sys.stdout.write(\"\\n\")\n    return 0\n\n\ndef _cmd_compare(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:\n    source_root = Path(args.source_root)\n    provenance = Path(args.provenance_map)\n    if not source_root.is_dir():\n        print(f\"error: source root not a directory: {source_root}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return 1\n    if not provenance.is_file():\n        print(f\"error: provenance map not found: {provenance}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return 1\n    try:\n        result = compare(source_root, provenance)\n    except ValueError as exc:\n        print(f\"error: {exc}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return 1\n    json.dump(result, sys.stdout, indent=2)\n    sys.stdout.write(\"\\n\")\n    return 0\n\n\ndef _build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(\n        prog=\"skf-hash-content\",\n        description=\"SHA-256 hashing helpers: single-file record or bulk-compare against provenance.\",\n    )\n    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest=\"cmd\", required=True)\n\n    p_hash = sub.add_parser(\"hash\", help=\"emit hash record for a single file\")\n    p_hash.add_argument(\"path\", help=\"path to the file\")\n    p_hash.add_argument(\n        \"--include-path\",\n        action=\"store_true\",\n        help=\"include the path string in the emitted record\",\n    )\n    p_hash.set_defaults(func=_cmd_hash)\n\n    p_cmp = sub.add_parser(\n        \"compare\",\n        help=\"classify provenance file_entries[] against current source tree\",\n    )\n    p_cmp.add_argument(\"source_root\", help=\"path to the source tree root\")\n    p_cmp.add_argument(\n        \"--provenance-map\",\n        required=True,\n        help=\"path to provenance-map.json (object with file_entries[] or bare array)\",\n    )\n    p_cmp.set_defaults(func=_cmd_compare)\n\n    return parser\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    parser = _build_parser()\n    args = parser.parse_args(argv)\n    return args.func(args)\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    raise SystemExit(main())\n"
}

  "new_string": "**Category D — Script/asset file changes:**\n\nRun the bulk comparison once via:\n\n```bash\nuv run {hashContentHelper} compare <source-root> \\\n    --provenance-map <provenance-map-path>\n```\n\nThe helper emits:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"comparisons\": [\n    {\"source_file\": \"...\", \"classification\": \"UNCHANGED|MODIFIED_FILE|DELETED_FILE\",\n     \"stored_hash\": \"sha256:...\", \"current_hash\": \"sha256:...\"|null,\n     \"current_size_bytes\": N|null}, ...\n  ],\n  \"stats\": {\"total\": N, \"unchanged\": U, \"modified\": M, \"deleted\": D}\n}\n```\n\nTranslate the helper's output into the change manifest:\n- `MODIFIED_FILE` rows → add to manifest as MODIFIED_FILE\n- `DELETED_FILE` rows → add to manifest as DELETED_FILE\n- `UNCHANGED` rows → omit from the manifest (no action needed)\n\nThe helper does NOT detect NEW_FILE — its job is provenance comparison only. Detect new files via `skf-detect-scripts-assets.py` from create-skill step 3 §4c against the current source tree, then subtract the paths already present in `provenance.file_entries[].source_file`. Remaining files matching detection patterns (`scripts/`, `bin/`, `assets/`, `templates/`) and NOT under `scripts/[MANUAL]/` or `assets/[MANUAL]/` are NEW_FILE.\n\nFiles in `scripts/[MANUAL]/` or `assets/[MANUAL]/` → SKIP (user-authored, preserved)."

64	### 3. Validate Brief Structure
65	
66	Check that the loaded skill-brief.yaml contains required fields:
67	
68	**Required fields:**
69	- `name` — skill identifier (kebab-case)
70	- `version` — source version to compile against
71	- `source_repo` — GitHub owner/repo or local path (**optional when `source_type: "docs-only"`**)
72	- `language` — primary source language
73	- `scope` — what to extract. Accepts either a string (simple scope description, e.g., "all public exports") or an object with sub-fields: `type` (e.g., `"component-library"`), `include`, `exclude`, `notes`, and optionally `demo_patterns`, `registry_path`, `ui_variants` for component libraries
74	
75	**Optional fields:**
76	- `source_type` — `"source"` (default) or `"docs-only"` (external documentation only)
77	- `doc_urls` — array of `{url, label}` documentation URLs (required when `source_type: "docs-only"`)
78	- `source_branch` — branch to use (default: main/master)
79	- `source_authority` — official/community/internal (default: community; forced to `community` for docs-only)
80	- `target_version` — specific version to compile against (triggers **explicit** tag resolution for remote repos; see source-resolution-protocols.md). When absent, the workflow falls back to **implicit** tag resolution from `brief.version` for remote sources — see below.
81	- `include_patterns` — file glob patterns to include
82	- `exclude_patterns` — file glob patterns to exclude
83	- `description` — human description of the skill
84	- `scripts_intent` — `"none"` to skip scripts detection, omit for default auto-detection
85	- `assets_intent` — `"none"` to skip assets detection, omit for default auto-detection
86	
87	**Docs-only validation:** When `source_type: "docs-only"`, `source_repo` is not required but `doc_urls` must have at least one entry. `source_authority` is forced to `community`.
88

90	Halt with specific error: "Brief validation failed: missing required field `{field}`. Update your skill-brief.yaml and re-run."

This matches the agentskills.io skill-name rule and the directory-name constraint that `skill-check`'s `frontmatter.name_matches_directory` rule will later enforce. If validation fails, halt BEFORE any directory is created or any path is resolved: "Brief validation failed: `name` field `{value}` does not match required pattern `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$`. Skill names must be 1-64 chars, lowercase alphanumeric plus hyphens, no leading hyphen, no underscores, no slashes. Update your skill-brief.yaml and re-run."
93	
94	**Version non-empty check:** reject `brief.version` if absent, empty, or whitespace-only (`version.strip() == ""`). Halt: "Brief validation failed: `version` field is required and must be non-empty. Update your skill-brief.yaml and re-run." This guards downstream directory resolution — an empty version would later create paths like `{skills_output_folder}/{name}//` with a stray double-slash, which is a nightmare to clean up.

104	- **Version-to-tag pinning intent:** If `brief.target_version` is absent but `brief.version` is present, record the intent to apply **implicit tag resolution** from `brief.version` when step 3 resolves the source. 108	- Store resolved: local path as `source_root`, file listing

  "content": "# /// script\n# requires-python = \">=3.10\"\n# dependencies = [\"pyyaml\", \"jsonschema>=4.0\"]\n# ///\n\"\"\"SKF Validate Brief Schema — schema check for a skill-brief.yaml on disk.\n\nLoads `skill-brief.yaml` from a path (or from stdin/inline-YAML), validates\nit against `src/shared/scripts/schemas/skill-brief.v1.json`, and applies the\ntwo conditional rules from `skf-create-skill/references/load-brief.md §3`\nthat the JSON schema doesn't express today:\n\n  - When `source_type == \"docs-only\"`: `doc_urls` must have ≥1 entry, and\n    `source_authority` must be `community` (the prose says it is \"forced\n    to community\" — we surface a warning when it disagrees rather than\n    silently rewriting).\n  - `version` must be present AND non-empty AND not whitespace-only. Calling stages can read `errors[]`\ndirectly and forward the `message` field to the user.\n\nCLI:\n  uv run skf-validate-brief-schema.py <path/to/skill-brief.yaml>\n  cat brief.yaml | uv run skf-validate-brief-schema.py -\n  uv run skf-validate-brief-schema.py --yaml '<inline yaml>'\n\nOutput (JSON on stdout):\n  {\n    \"valid\": bool,\n    \"errors\":   [{\"field\": \"...\", \"message\": \"...\"}, ...],\n    \"warnings\": [{\"field\": \"...\", \"message\": \"...\"}, ...],\n    \"halt_reason\": \"brief-missing\" | \"brief-malformed\" | \"brief-invalid\" | null,\n    \"brief\": { ...parsed YAML if loadable, else null... }\n  }\n\nExit codes:\n  0 — valid (errors empty)\n  1 — invalid (errors non-empty) OR file/yaml load failed\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport json\nimport sys\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Any\n\nimport yaml\nfrom jsonschema import Draft202012Validator\n\n\nREPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent.parent\nSCHEMA_PATH = (\n    REPO_ROOT / \"src\" / \"shared\" / \"scripts\" / \"schemas\" / \"skill-brief.v1.json\"\n)\n\n\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Loading\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef load_schema() -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Read the skill-brief schema from its canonical path.\"\"\"\n    return json.loads(SCHEMA_PATH.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n\n\ndef load_brief_text(text: str) -> tuple[dict | None, str | None]:\n    \"\"\"Parse YAML text. Returns (brief, error_message).\"\"\"\n    try:\n        brief = yaml.safe_load(text)\n    except yaml.YAMLError as exc:\n        return None, f\"Brief is not valid YAML: {exc}\"\n    if brief is None:\n        return None, \"Brief is empty\"\n    if not isinstance(brief, dict):\n        return None, f\"Brief must be a YAML mapping; Update your skill-brief.yaml and re-run.\"\n            ),\n        }\n    if validator == \"minLength\":\n        return {\n            \"field\": field,\n            \"message\": (\n                f\"Brief validation failed: `{field}` field must be non-empty. \"\n                f\"Update your skill-brief.yaml and re-run.\"\n            ),\n        }\n    if validator == \"minItems\":\n        return {\n            \"field\": field,\n            \"message\": (\n                f\"Brief validation failed: `{field}` field must contain at least \"\n                f\"{err.validator_value} item(s). --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef _docs_only_rules(brief: dict) -> tuple[list[dict], list[dict]]:\n    \"\"\"Apply the docs-only conditional rules.\n\n    Returns (errors, warnings).\n    \"\"\"\n    errors: list[dict] = []\n    warnings: list[dict] = []\n    if brief.get(\"source_type\") != \"docs-only\":\n        return errors, errors.extend(cond_errors)\n    warnings.extend(cond_warnings)\n\n    errors.extend(_version_non_empty_rule(brief))\n\n    return {\n        \"valid\": not errors,\n        \"errors\": errors,\n return {\n        \"valid\": False,\n        \"errors\": errors,\n        \"warnings\": warnings,\n        \"halt_reason\": \"brief-invalid\",\n        \"brief\": brief,\n    }\n\n\ndef _envelope_valid(brief: dict, warnings: list[dict]) -> dict:\n    return {\n        \"valid\": True,\n        \"errors\": [],\n        \"warnings\": warnings,\n        \"halt_reason\": None,\n        \"brief\": brief,\n    }\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(\n        prog=\"skf-validate-brief-schema\",\n        description=\"Validate a skill-brief.yaml against the SKF brief schema.\",\n    )\n    src = parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group(required=True)\n    src.add_argument(\n        \"path\",\n        nargs=\"?\",\n        help=\"path to skill-brief.yaml; pass `-` to read from stdin\",\n    )\n    src.add_argument(\n        \"--yaml\",\n        dest=\"inline_yaml\",\n        help=\"inline YAML text to validate (alternative to a path)\",\n    )\n    args = parser.parse_args(argv)\n\n    if args.inline_yaml is not None:\n        text = args.inline_yaml\n    elif args.path == \"-\":\n        text = sys.stdin.read()\n    else:\n        brief_path = Path(args.path)\n        if not brief_path.is_file():\n            _emit(\n                _envelope_load_error(\n                    \"brief-missing\",\n                    f\"Brief not found at `{brief_path}`. Run [BS] Brief Skill to \"\n                    \"create one, or use [QS] Quick Skill for brief-less generation.\",\n                )\n            )\n            return 1\n        text = brief_path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n\n    brief, load_err = load_brief_text(text)\n    if load_err is not None:\n        _emit(_envelope_load_error(\"brief-malformed\", load_err))\n        return 1\n    assert brief is not None\n\n    result = validate_brief(brief)\n    if not result[\"valid\"]:\n        _emit(_envelope_invalid(brief, result[\"errors\"], result[\"warnings\"]))\n        return 1\n\n    _emit(_envelope_valid(brief, result[\"warnings\"]))\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    raise SystemExit(main())\n"
}

Accepts either a string (simple scope description, e.g., \"all public exports\") or an object with sub-fields: `type` (e.g., `\"component-library\"`), `include`, `exclude`, `notes`, and optionally `demo_patterns`, `registry_path`, `ui_variants` for component libraries\n\n**Optional fields:**\n- `source_type` — `\"source\"` (default) or `\"docs-only\"` (external documentation only)\n- `doc_urls` — array of `{url, label}` documentation URLs (required when `source_type: \"docs-only\"`)\n- `source_branch` — branch to use (default: main/master)\n- `source_authority` — official/community/internal (default: community; forced to `community` for docs-only)\n- `target_version` — specific version to compile against (triggers **explicit** tag resolution for remote repos; see source-resolution-protocols.md). When absent, the workflow falls back to **implicit** tag resolution from `brief.version` for remote sources — see below.\n- `include_patterns` — file glob patterns to include\n- `exclude_patterns` — file glob patterns to exclude\n- `description` — human description of the skill\n- `scripts_intent` — `\"none\"` to skip scripts detection, omit for default auto-detection\n- `assets_intent` — `\"none\"` to skip assets detection, omit for default auto-detection\n\n**Docs-only validation:** When `source_type: \"docs-only\"`, `source_repo` is not required but `doc_urls` must have at least one entry. `source_authority` is forced to `community`.\n\n**If required fields missing:**\nHalt with specific error: \"Brief validation failed: missing required field `{field}`. Update your skill-brief.yaml and re-run.\"\n\n**Name format check (run after required-field check, before any path creation):** validate `brief.name` against the regex `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$` — 1-64 characters, lowercase alphanumeric plus hyphens, must start with a letter or digit, no leading hyphen, no uppercase, no underscores, no slashes. This matches the agentskills.io skill-name rule and the directory-name constraint that `skill-check`'s `frontmatter.name_matches_directory` rule will later enforce. If validation fails, halt BEFORE any directory is created or any path is resolved: \"Brief validation failed: `name` field `{value}` does not match required pattern `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$`. Skill names must be 1-64 chars, lowercase alphanumeric plus hyphens, no leading hyphen, no underscores, no slashes. Update your skill-brief.yaml and re-run.\"\n\n**Version non-empty check:** reject `brief.version` if absent, empty, or whitespace-only (`version.strip() == \"\"`). Halt: \"Brief validation failed: `version` field is required and must be non-empty. Update your skill-brief.yaml and re-run.\" This guards downstream directory resolution — an empty version would later create paths like `{skills_output_folder}/{name}//` with a stray double-slash, which is a nightmare to clean up.",
  "new_string": "### 3. Validate Brief Structure\n\nRun the deterministic schema validator — it checks required fields, regex patterns (`name`, `version`), enum membership (`source_type`, `source_authority`, `forge_tier`, `scope.type`), type correctness, the docs-only conditional rule (`doc_urls` ≥ 1 when `source_type == \"docs-only\"`), and the version-non-empty-or-whitespace rule:\n\n```bash\nuv run {validateBriefSchemaHelper} <path-to-skill-brief.yaml>\n```\n\nThe helper emits:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"valid\": <bool>,\n  \"errors\":   [{\"field\": \"...\", \"message\": \"Brief validation failed: ...\"}, ...],\n  \"warnings\": [{\"field\": \"...\", \"message\": \"...\"}, ...],\n  \"halt_reason\": \"brief-missing\" | \"brief-malformed\" | \"brief-invalid\" | null,\n  \"brief\": { ...parsed YAML when loadable... }\n}\n```\n\n**If `valid` is false:** HALT and display the first error's `message` field verbatim — the helper already formats messages in the \"Brief validation failed: ...\" form the user expects. For halt-reasons:\n\n- `brief-missing` — the brief path doesn't exist. Display the helper's message (it includes the `Run [BS] Brief Skill` redirect).\n- `brief-malformed` — the YAML failed to parse. Display the helper's message.\n- `brief-invalid` — schema or conditional-rule violation. Display the first `errors[].message`. Multiple errors may appear; the user typically fixes one source and re-runs.\n\n**If `valid` is true:** continue with `brief` (the parsed object) for downstream sections. Surface any `warnings[]` to the user but do not halt.\n\n**Field reference (for human readers):**\n\nThe complete contract — required fields, optional fields, types, and rules — lives in `src/shared/scripts/schemas/skill-brief.v1.json` and the prose mirror at `src/skf-brief-skill/assets/skill-brief-schema.md`. Read those if you need to explain a specific field; do NOT restate the rules here."

A9 done — plus a regression fix I caught while running tests: `package.json`'s `test:python` was silently omitting the three prior PRs' test suites (description-guard, detect-scripts-assets, hash-content). All four are now wired in. **CI Python suite jumped from 796 → 927 tests across 27 files.**

Worth saving as memory: the `test:python` omission is the kind of "tests exist but aren't running in CI" gap that flowed straight from the merge-cadence and recall the `feedback_release_pipeline_e2e_validation.md` lesson. Let me save it.

  "content": "---\nname: test-python-must-include-new-suites\ndescription: When adding a new Python test file under test/, also update package.json's test:python script — pytest only runs files explicitly listed there\nmetadata:\n  type: feedback\n---\n\nWhen adding a new `test/test-skf-*.py` file in this repo, also append it to the `test:python` script in `package.json`. The script enumerates every test file by path; pytest does NOT auto-discover, and adding a test without wiring it leaves it dormant — present in the tree but never run.\n\n**Why:** Discovered during A9 (PR #311) that PRs #308 (description-guard), #309 (detect-scripts-assets), and #310 (hash-content) had each added their test suite to `test/` but skipped the `package.json` update. All three were sitting in the tree unused since their merge. The pre-commit hook runs the listed file set, so the local `pytest` runs the author did pre-merge succeeded — but CI was silently dropping them. Caught only because A9's new dep (`jsonschema`) forced me to re-read the test:python command line and notice the missing entries. This is exactly the [[feedback_release_pipeline_e2e_validation]] pattern (tests exist but aren't running in the path that matters) one layer down.\n\n**How to apply:** When committing a new test file:\n1. Add it to `test:python`'s positional pytest args in `package.json` (the long single-line command at the end of the test scripts block)\n2. If the new test pulls in a Python dep beyond pyyaml/pytest (jsonschema, requests, etc.), add `--with <pkg>` to the `uv run` invocation in the same line\n3. Re-run `npm run test:python` and confirm the new file's test count appears in the summary\n4. Don't rely on `pytest test/` auto-discovery — the project deliberately enumerates so that test deps can be declared per-invocation via `uv run --with`\n\nSame applies to `test/test-*.js` Node tests (each has its own npm script).\n"
}

> AGENT

Found it. Two root causes:

1. **Path separator leak** in `skf-detect-scripts-assets.py`: `str(path.relative_to(source_root))` produces `scripts\deploy.sh` on Windows. Production bug — JSON output should be platform-independent (forward-slash form).

2. **CRLF newline translation** in test fixtures: `path.write_text(content)` translates `\n` → `\r\n` on Windows, so `b"x\n"` becomes `b"x\r\n"` on disk — `size_bytes` and SHA-256 diverge from what tests expect. Test-fixture bug — need `newline=""` to preserve exact bytes.

Both surfaced because PR #311 was the first to actually run these tests on Windows CI (they weren't wired into `test:python` before this PR). Fixing on this same branch.

> TOOL

tool_use Edit
id: toolu_01XAQG5vbrrhy3ga9FQNJLbS
```json
{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/home/armel/Projects/OSS/bmad-module-skill-forge/src/shared/scripts/skf-detect-scripts-assets.py",
  "old_string": "def matches_scope(path: Path, root: Path, scope_patterns: list[str]) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Match `path` against scope-include glob patterns relative to root.\"\"\"\n    if not scope_patterns:\n        return True\n    rel = str(path.relative_to(root))\n    return any(fnmatch.fnmatch(rel, pattern) for pattern in scope_patterns)",
  "new_string": "def matches_scope(path: Path, root: Path, scope_patterns: list[str]) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Match `path` against scope-include glob patterns relative to root.\n\n    Forward-slash form so scope patterns like \"scripts/*\" match on Windows\n    too — fnmatch is byte-exact and won't normalize separators for us.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not scope_patterns:\n        return True\n    rel = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()\n    return any(fnmatch.fnmatch(rel, pattern) for pattern in scope_patterns)"
}

All 7 checks green — windows-latest python passed at 1m27s. PR #311 is ready to merge.

## Summary of fixes pushed to PR #311

Three commits resolved the Windows CI failures:

| Commit | Class | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `d6b4de5d` | Production | `skf-detect-scripts-assets.py` — `path.relative_to(root).as_posix()` in `build_*_record` + `matches_scope` (fnmatch is byte-exact on separators). `skf-hash-content.py` — `path.as_posix()` in `--include-path` output. |
| `d6b4de5d` | Test fixture | `write_file` / `_write` switched to `write_bytes(content.encode())` — Windows text-mode write was translating `\n` → `\r\n`, corrupting `size_bytes` and SHA-256 vs the expected values. |
| `21e9470f` | Test assertion | The two `--include-path` tests asserting `rec["path"] == str(path)` updated to `path.as_posix()` to match the new contract. |

**Net effect:** all 927 tests now pass on both `ubuntu-latest` AND `windows-latest`. Two pre-existing cross-platform bugs in PRs #309 and #310 were exposed only because PR #311 was the first to wire those test files into `test:python` — exactly the [test:python must include new suites](feedback_test_python_must_include_new_suites.md) memory pattern paying off in retrospect.

  "content": "# /// script\n# requires-python = \">=3.10\"\n# dependencies = []\n# ///\n\"\"\"SKF Check Workspace Drift — pre-flight guard for gap-driven update-skill runs.\n\n`skf-update-skill/references/re-extract.md §0.a` defines a four-state guard:\nthe workspace at `source_root` must point at the commit the skill was pinned\nagainst (`metadata.source_commit`), otherwise gap-driven spot-checks read\nbytes that differ from the pinned tree and silently produce wrong results\n(symbols appear \"verified\" because the recorded line now points at different\ncode).\n\nThe guard's logic is deterministic — three git commands and a comparison —\nbut the prose form asked the LLM to chain them per run, with subtle short-\nSHA prefix matching and skip-paths for non-git workspaces. This script bakes\nthe dispatch in.\n\nCLI:\n  uv run skf-check-workspace-drift.py <source-root> \\\\\n      --pinned-commit <SHA or empty> \\\\\n      [--source-ref <ref>] \\\\\n      [--allow-drift]\n\nInputs:\n  source_root       Filesystem path to the workspace under test.\n  --pinned-commit   The pinned commit SHA (full or short). Pass an empty\n                    string OR the literal \"local\" to declare that this\n                    skill has no pinned commit — the guard skips with\n                    skip_reason=\"no-pinned-commit\".\n  --source-ref      Optional. The ref name (tag, branch) the workspace\n                    was pinned to. Mismatches still return\n                    status=\"overridden\" so the caller can surface a\n                    warning in the final report.\n\nOutput (JSON on stdout):\n  {\n    \"status\": \"ok\" | \"skipped\" | \"mismatch\" | \"overridden\",\n    \"skip_reason\": \"no-pinned-commit\" | \"not-a-git-tree\" | null,\n    \"pinned_commit\": \"<as-given>\",\n    \"head_sha\": \"<full SHA>\" | null,\n    \"head_short_sha\": \"<7-12 chars>\" | null,\n    \"match_kind\": \"full\" | \"short-prefix\" | null,\n    \"log_message\": \"workspace_drift_check: ok (abc1234)\",\n    \"halt_message\": \"<multi-line user-facing message>\" | null\n  }\n\nExit codes:\n  0  — caller may continue (status is ok, skipped, or overridden)\n  1  — script error (bad args, source_root missing, git unavailable)\n  2  — drift detected and --allow-drift was NOT passed; caller MUST halt\n       with status=\"halted-for-workspace-drift\". The halt_message field\n       is pre-formatted with all substitutions applied.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport json\nimport shutil\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\n\nSKIP_NO_PINNED = \"no-pinned-commit\"\nSKIP_NOT_GIT = \"not-a-git-tree\"\n\n\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Git probes\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef _git(args: list[str], *, cwd: Path) -> tuple[int, str, str]:\n    \"\"\"Run a git command; return (rc, stdout, stderr). Stdout/stderr stripped.\"\"\"\n    proc = subprocess.run(\n        [\"git\", \"-C\", str(cwd), *args],\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        check=False,\n    )\n    return proc.returncode, proc.stdout.strip(), proc.stderr.strip()\n\n\ndef is_git_working_tree(source_root: Path) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"True if `git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree` says yes.\"\"\"\n    rc, out, _ = _git([\"rev-parse\", \"--is-inside-work-tree\"], cwd=source_root)\n    return rc == 0 and out == \"true\"\n\n\ndef head_sha(source_root: Path) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the workspace HEAD SHA, or None if it can't be read.\"\"\"\n    rc, out, _ = _git([\"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\"], cwd=source_root)\n    if rc != 0 or not out:\n        return None\n    return out\n\n\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Match logic\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef is_skippable_pinned(pinned_commit: str) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Recognize the scalar values that mean 'no pinned commit'.\"\"\"\n    if pinned_commit is None:\n        return True\n    stripped = pinned_commit.strip()\n    return stripped == \"\" or stripped.lower() == \"local\"\n\n\ndef classify_match(pinned: str, head: str) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Return 'full' if pinned == head, 'short-prefix' if pinned is a prefix\n    of head (≥ 7 chars to avoid coincidental collisions on short SHAs).\n    Returns None on no match.\"\"\"\n    if pinned == head:\n        return \"full\"\n    if len(pinned) >= 7 and head.startswith(pinned):\n        return \"short-prefix\"\n    return None\n\n\ndef short(sha: str) -> str:\n    return sha[:7]\n\n\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Halt message\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\nHALT_MESSAGE_TEMPLATE = \"\"\"Workspace HEAD does not match the commit this skill was pinned against.\n\n  pinned (metadata.source_commit): {pinned_commit}\n  pinned ref (metadata.source_ref): {source_ref}\n  workspace HEAD ({source_root}):  {head_sha}\n\nGap-driven spot-checks read source at pinned line numbers — verifying\nagainst a drifted tree silently produces wrong results (symbols appear at\nunintended locations). Re-sync the workspace before re-running:\n\n  git -C \"{source_root}\" checkout {checkout_target}\n\nOr, to intentionally proceed against the current workspace HEAD (accepting\nthat spot-checks will read bytes that differ from the pinned commit),\nre-run update-skill with `--allow-workspace-drift`.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef build_halt_message(\n    *, source_root: Path, pinned_commit: str, head_sha_full: str, source_ref: str | None\n) -> str:\n    ref_display = source_ref if source_ref else \"unset\"\n    checkout_target = source_ref if source_ref else pinned_commit\n    return HALT_MESSAGE_TEMPLATE.format(\n        pinned_commit=pinned_commit,\n        source_ref=ref_display,\n        source_root=str(source_root),\n        head_sha=head_sha_full,\n        checkout_target=checkout_target,\n    )\n\n\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Core check\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef check(\n    source_root: Path,\n    *,\n    pinned_commit: str,\n    source_ref: str | None,\n    allow_drift: bool,\n) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Run the four-state guard and return a result envelope.\"\"\"\n    if is_skippable_pinned(pinned_commit):\n        return {\n            \"status\": \"skipped\",\n            \"skip_reason\": SKIP_NO_PINNED,\n            \"pinned_commit\": pinned_commit,\n            \"head_sha\": None,\n            \"head_short_sha\": None,\n            \"match_kind\": None,\n            \"log_message\": \"workspace_drift_check: skipped (no pinned commit)\",\n            \"halt_message\": None,\n        }\n\n    if not is_git_working_tree(source_root):\n        return {\n            \"status\": \"skipped\",\n            \"skip_reason\": SKIP_NOT_GIT,\n            \"pinned_commit\": pinned_commit,\n            \"head_sha\": None,\n            \"head_short_sha\": None,\n            \"match_kind\": None,\n            \"log_message\": \"workspace_drift_check: skipped (not a git working tree)\",\n            \"halt_message\": None,\n        }\n\n    head = head_sha(source_root)\n    if head is None:\n        # git tree exists but HEAD can't be resolved (orphan / empty repo).\n        # Treat as not-a-git-tree for guard purposes — we can't verify pinning.\n        return {\n            \"status\": \"skipped\",\n            \"skip_reason\": SKIP_NOT_GIT,\n            \"pinned_commit\": pinned_commit,\n            \"head_sha\": None,\n            \"head_short_sha\": None,\n            \"match_kind\": None,\n            \"log_message\": \"workspace_drift_check: skipped (HEAD unreadable)\",\n            \"halt_message\": None,\n        }\n\n    match_kind = classify_match(pinned_commit, head)\n    if match_kind is not None:\n        return {\n            \"status\": \"ok\",\n            \"skip_reason\": None,\n            \"pinned_commit\": pinned_commit,\n            \"head_sha\": head,\n            \"head_short_sha\": short(head),\n            \"match_kind\": match_kind,\n            \"log_message\": f\"workspace_drift_check: ok ({short(head)})\",\n            \"halt_message\": None,\n        }\n\n    # Mismatch path\n    halt_message = build_halt_message(\n        source_root=source_root,\n        pinned_commit=pinned_commit,\n        head_sha_full=head,\n        source_ref=source_ref,\n    )\n    if allow_drift:\n        return {\n            \"status\": \"overridden\",\n            \"skip_reason\": None,\n            \"pinned_commit\": pinned_commit,\n            \"head_sha\": head,\n            \"head_short_sha\": short(head),\n            \"match_kind\": None,\n            \"log_message\": (\n                f\"workspace_drift_check: overridden \"\n                f\"(pinned={pinned_commit}, head={head})\"\n            ),\n            \"halt_message\": halt_message,  # surfaced as warning by caller\n        }\n\n    return {\n        \"status\": \"mismatch\",\n        \"skip_reason\": None,\n        \"pinned_commit\": pinned_commit,\n        \"head_sha\": head,\n        \"head_short_sha\": short(head),\n        \"match_kind\": None,\n        \"log_message\": (\n            f\"workspace_drift_check: mismatch \"\n            f\"(pinned={pinned_commit}, head={head})\"\n        ),\n        \"halt_message\": halt_message,\n    }\n\n\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# CLI\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(\n        prog=\"skf-check-workspace-drift\",\n        description=(\n            \"Verify that the source-root workspace HEAD matches the pinned \"\n            \"commit recorded in metadata.source_commit.\"\n        ),\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\"source_root\", help=\"path to the workspace under test\")\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"--pinned-commit\",\n        required=True,\n        help='pinned commit SHA; pass \"\" or \"local\" to skip the guard',\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"--source-ref\",\n        default=None,\n        help=\"optional pinned ref (tag/branch) for halt-message display\",\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"--allow-drift\",\n        action=\"store_true\",\n        help=\"suppress the drift halt; mismatch becomes status=overridden\",\n    )\n    args = parser.parse_args(argv)\n\n    source_root = Path(args.source_root)\n    if not source_root.is_dir():\n        print(f\"error: source-root not a directory: {source_root}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return 1\n    if shutil.which(\"git\") is None:\n        print(\"error: git binary not on PATH\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return 1\n\n    result = check(\n        source_root,\n        pinned_commit=args.pinned_commit,\n        source_ref=args.source_ref,\n        allow_drift=args.allow_drift,\n    )\n    json.dump(result, sys.stdout, indent=2)\n    sys.stdout.write(\"\\n\")\n    if result[\"status\"] == \"mismatch\":\n        return 2\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    raise SystemExit(main())\n"
}

62	def _create_symlink_or_junction(target: str, link_path: Path) -> str:
63	    """Create a directory link from link_path to target.
64	
65	    On POSIX: standard symlink. On Windows: try symlink first (works under
66	    Developer Mode or admin), fall back to a directory junction via `mklink /J`
67	    on PRIVILEGE_NOT_HELD / ACCESS_DENIED. Junctions don't need elevation and
68	    behave like directory symlinks for the resolve() / is_dir() consumers in
69	    skf-skill-inventory.py.
70	
71	    Returns "symlink" or "junction" so callers can report which kind was made.
72	    """
73	    try:
74	        os.symlink(target, link_path)
75	        return "symlink"
76	    except OSError as e:
77	        if os.name != "nt" or getattr(e, "winerror", None) not in (1314, 5):
78	            raise
79	        # Junctions are absolute-path-only and target must be a real directory
80	        # at creation time. Resolve relative `target` against link_path's parent.
81	        abs_target = (link_path.parent / target).resolve()
82	        if not abs_target.is_dir():
83	            raise OSError(
84	                errno.ENOTDIR,
85	                f"junction fallback requires existing directory target: {abs_target}",
86	            ) from e
87	        result = subprocess.run(
88	            ["cmd", "/c", "mklink", "/J", str(link_path), str(abs_target)],
89	            capture_output=True,
90	            text=True,
91	            timeout=30,
92	        )
93	        if result.returncode != 0:
94	            raise OSError(
95	                e.errno,
96	                f"junction fallback failed: {result.stderr.strip() or result.stdout.strip()}",
97	            ) from e
98	        return "junction"

102	    """Acquire an exclusive non-blocking lock on fd (auto-released on close/exit)."""
103	    if os.name == "nt":
104	        try:
105	            msvcrt.locking(fd, msvcrt.LK_NBLCK, 1)
106	        except OSError as e:
107	            if e.errno in (errno.EAGAIN, errno.EACCES, errno.EDEADLK):
108	                raise OSError(errno.EAGAIN, "lock held") from e
109	            raise

Log the message to the evidence report.\n\n**Dispatch on `status`:**\n\n- **`ok`** (exit 0): symlink already points at `{version}` — no disk write. Continue to §6.\n- **`flipped`** (exit 0): symlink was atomically updated (temp-and-replace). Continue to §6.\n- **`missing-target`** (exit 2): `{skill_group}/{version}/` directory does not exist on disk. HALT — display `halt_message` verbatim. This indicates §4 §6b did not write the version directory before §5b ran (a workflow bug, not a user error).\n- **`mismatch`** (exit 2): re-read after flip showed the symlink still points elsewhere. HALT — display `halt_message`. 293	#### 2.2 — Major-Version Scope Reconciliation (Post-Detection)
294	
295	**Purpose:** §1c catches the major-version case when an audit drift report supplies explicit candidates. §2.2 is the safety net that fires when no audit was run (or audit emitted no out-of-scope section): it inspects the just-built Category A/B results for the deletion-ratio signature of a major-version restructure and gives the user an off-ramp before §3 commits the change manifest.

300	- `degraded_mode == true` (no provenance baseline to compare against — every export looks "modified", deletion ratio is meaningless), OR

303	**Trigger:** Compute
304	
305	```
306	deleted_export_count = (sum of exports across Category A DELETED files)
307	                     + (DELETED_EXPORT count from Category B)
308	total_provenance_exports = provenance_map.entries.length
309	deletion_ratio = deleted_export_count / total_provenance_exports
310	```

312	If `deletion_ratio >= 0.50`, present the prompt below. Otherwise skip §2.2 silently and continue to §3.

321	Added files (in scope): {added_in_scope_count}

328	[B] Brief    — halt and re-run skf-brief-skill to refine scope first

330	```

A non-interactive run must not silently halt, but the user must be able to see the signal post-hoc.

list,\n    a_deleted: list,\n    c_renamed_files: list,\n    b_modified: list,\n    b_new: list,\n    b_deleted: list,\n    b_moved: list,\n) -> list[dict]:\n    \"\"\"Group exports under their owning file path. Preserves stable ordering:\n    MODIFIED files first, then ADDED, then DELETED, then MOVED. Files within\n    each status sorted alphabetically by path.\"\"\"\n    exports_by_file: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}\n\n    def _record(entry: dict, change_type: str) -> None:\n        path = entry.get(\"file\")\n        if not path:\n            return\n        exports_by_file.setdefault(path, []).append({\n            \"name\": entry.get(\"name\"),\n            \"change_type\": change_type,\n            \"old_line\": entry.get(\"old_line\"),\n            \"new_line\": entry.get(\"new_line\") or entry.get(\"line\"),\n        })\n\n    for e in b_modified:\n        _record(e, \"MODIFIED_EXPORT\")\n    for e in b_new:\n        _record(e, \"NEW_EXPORT\")\n    for e in b_deleted:\n        _record(e, \"DELETED_EXPORT\")\n    for e in b_moved:\n        _record(e, \"MOVED_EXPORT\")\n\n    out: list[dict] = []\n\n    for path in sorted(a_modified):\n        out.append({\n            \"file_path\": path,\n            \"status\": \"MODIFIED\",\n            \"exports_affected\": exports_by_file.get(path, []),\n        })\n\n    for path in sorted(a_added):\n        out.append({\n            \"file_path\": path,\n            \"status\": \"ADDED\",\n            \"exports_affected\": exports_by_file.get(path, []),\n        })\n\n    for path in sorted(a_deleted):\n        out.append({\n            \"file_path\": path,\n            \"status\": \"DELETED\",\n            \"exports_affected\": exports_by_file.get(path, []),\n        })\n\n    # MOVED entries from Category C — emit one record per move with the new path\n    for move in sorted(c_renamed_files, key=lambda m: m.get(\"new_path\") or \"\"):\n        new_path = move.get(\"new_path\")\n        if new_path is None:\n            continue\n        out.append({\n            \"file_path\": new_path,\n            \"status\": \"MOVED\",\n            \"old_path\": move.get(\"old_path\"),\n            \"exports_affected\": exports_by_file.get(new_path, []),\n        })\n\n    return out\n\n\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Deletion ratio (§2.2)\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef compute_deletion_ratio(payload: dict, provenance: dict) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Compute the §2.2 deletion-ratio trigger envelope.\n\n    Skip conditions (per the §2.2 prose):\n      - update_mode == \"gap-driven\"\n      - degraded_mode is True\n      - provenance has zero entries (denominator would be zero)\n    \"\"\"\n    if payload.get(\"update_mode\") == \"gap-driven\":\n        return _ratio_skip(skip_reason=\"gap-driven\")\n    if payload.get(\"degraded_mode\"):\n        return _ratio_skip(skip_reason=\"degraded-mode\")\n\n    entries = provenance.get(\"entries\", [])\n    if not isinstance(entries, list):\n        raise ValueError(\"provenance `entries` must be an array\")\n    total = len(entries)\n    if total == 0:\n        return _ratio_skip(skip_reason=\"zero-provenance-exports\")\n\n    # Count exports under category A deleted files (via provenance lookup)\n    by_source: dict[str, int] = {}\n    for entry in entries:\n        sf = entry.get(\"source_file\")\n        if isinstance(sf, str):\n            by_source[sf] = by_source.get(sf, 0) + 1\n\n    cat_a = payload.get(\"category_a\", {}) or {}\n    deleted_files = _get_list(cat_a, \"deleted\")\n    deleted_in_files = sum(by_source.get(p, 0) for p in deleted_files)\n\n    cat_b = payload.get(\"category_b\", {}) or {}\n    deleted_exports = len(_get_list(cat_b, \"deleted_exports\"))\n\n    deleted_export_count = deleted_in_files + deleted_exports\n    ratio = deleted_export_count / total\n\n    cat_c = payload.get(\"category_c\", {}) or {}\n    renamed_or_moved = (\n        len(_get_list(cat_c, \"renamed_files\"))\n        + len(_get_list(cat_b, \"moved_exports\"))\n        + len(_get_list(cat_c, \"renamed_exports\"))\n    )\n\n    return {\n        \"skip_reason\": None,\n        \"deleted_export_count\": deleted_export_count,\n        \"total_provenance_exports\": total,\n        \"deletion_ratio\": ratio,\n        \"deleted_file_count\": len(deleted_files),\n        \"added_in_scope_count\": len(_get_list(cat_a, \"added\")),\n        \"renamed_or_moved_count\": renamed_or_moved,\n        \"should_trigger\": ratio >= 0.50,\n    }\n\n\ndef _ratio_skip(*, skip_reason: str) -> dict:\n    return {\n        \"skip_reason\": skip_reason,\n        \"deleted_export_count\": 0,\n        \"total_provenance_exports\": 0,\n        \"deletion_ratio\": 0.0,\n        \"deleted_file_count\": 0,\n        \"added_in_scope_count\": 0,\n        \"renamed_or_moved_count\": 0,\n        \"should_trigger\": False,\n    }\n\n\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# CLI\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef _cmd_build(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:\n    try:\n        payload = _load_input(Path(args.input) if args.input else None)\n    except ValueError as exc:\n        print(f\"error: {exc}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return 1\n    manifest = build_manifest(payload)\n    json.dump(manifest, sys.stdout, indent=2)\n    sys.stdout.write(\"\\n\")\n    return 0\n\n\ndef _cmd_deletion_ratio(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:\n    try:\n        payload = _load_input(Path(args.input) if args.input else None)\n    except ValueError as exc:\n        print(f\"error: {exc}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return 1\n    prov_path = Path(args.provenance_map)\n    if not prov_path.is_file():\n        print(f\"error: provenance-map not found: {prov_path}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return 1\n    try:\n        provenance = json.loads(prov_path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:\n        print(f\"error: provenance-map is not valid JSON: {exc}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return 1\n    try:\n        result = compute_deletion_ratio(payload, provenance)\n    except ValueError as exc:\n        print(f\"error: {exc}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return 1\n    json.dump(result, sys.stdout, indent=2)\n    sys.stdout.write(\"\\n\")\n    return 0\n\n\ndef _build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(\n        prog=\"skf-build-change-manifest\",\n        description=(\n            \"Aggregate category A/B/C/D detection results into the unified \"\n            \"change manifest, OR compute the §2.2 deletion-ratio trigger.\"\n        ),\n    )\n    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest=\"cmd\", required=True)\n\n    p_build = sub.add_parser(\"build\", help=\"aggregate categories into manifest\")\n    p_build.add_argument(\n        \"--input\", default=None, help=\"path to JSON input (default: stdin)\"\n    )\n    p_build.set_defaults(func=_cmd_build)\n\n    p_ratio = sub.add_parser(\n        \"deletion-ratio\",\n        help=\"compute §2.2 trigger; requires --provenance-map\",\n    )\n    p_ratio.add_argument(\n        \"--input\", default=None, help=\"path to JSON input (default: stdin)\"\n    )\n    p_ratio.add_argument(\n        \"--provenance-map\", required=True, help=\"path to provenance-map.json\"\n    )\n    p_ratio.set_defaults(func=_cmd_deletion_ratio)\n\n    return parser\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    parser = _build_parser()\n    args = parser.parse_args(argv)\n    return args.func(args)\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    raise SystemExit(main())\n"
}

not found\" in result.stderr\n\n    def test_deletion_ratio_malformed_provenance_exits_1(self, tmp_path: Path) -> None:\n        prov = tmp_path / \"prov.json\"\n        prov.write_text(\"{not json\", valid JSON\" in result.stderr\n\n    def test_no_subcommand_exits_2(self) -> None:\n        result = _run_cli()\n        assert result.returncode == 2  # argparse missing required subparser\n"

Without it, update-skill silently misses the new surface and pays the gap cost on every future update — the cocoindex `0.3.37 → 1.0.0` and cognee `0.5.8 → 1.0.0` runs are existence proofs that this case is real and recurring.

209:     2. Append a `brief.scope.amendments[]` entry: `action: "skipped"`, `category: "scope-expansion"`, `path: candidate.path`, `reason: {user-provided or auto: "user declined promotion at update-skill §1c"}`, `evidence: {evidence string}`, `date: {today ISO}`, `workflow: "skf-update-skill"`.

303:**Purpose:** §1c catches the major-version case when an audit drift report supplies explicit candidates. §2.2 is the safety net that fires when no audit was run (or audit emitted no out-of-scope section): it inspects the just-built Category A/B results for the deletion-ratio signature of a major-version restructure and gives the user an off-ramp before §3 commits the change manifest.
353:- **[A] Audit:** halt with status `halted-for-audit`. Display: `"Halting update-skill. Run skf-audit-skill against {skill_name} to map the new surface — its drift report will feed §1c on the next update-skill run."` Change manifest discarded.
355:**Why both §1c and §2.2:** §1c is precise (per-path P/S/U) but requires upstream signal from audit-skill. §2.2 is coarse (single halt/continue) but self-contained — it fires even when the user runs update-skill directly without audit. 152	### 1c. Major-Version Scope Reconciliation (Pre-Detection)
153	
154	**Purpose:** When upstream undergoes a paradigm shift (rebrand, package restructure, major-version rewrite), the brief's `scope.include` no longer reflects the real public API. §1b handles new authoritative-doc files; §1c handles new **code globs** that fall outside the original scope. Without it, update-skill silently misses the new surface and pays the gap cost on every future update — the cocoindex `0.3.37 → 1.0.0` and cognee `0.5.8 → 1.0.0` runs are existence proofs that this case is real and recurring.
155	
156	**Skip this section entirely if:**
157	
158	- `update_mode == "gap-driven"` (test-report mode — source hasn't drifted), OR
159	- `metadata.json.source_type == "docs-only"` (no source tree to scope), OR
160	- No audit drift report is available at the path computed in step 1 below.
161	
162	**Procedure:**
163	
164	1. **Locate the most recent audit drift report.** Search `{forge_data_folder}/{skill_name}/{baseline_version}/drift-report-*.md`, sorted by timestamp descending. Pick the latest. If none found, **skip §1c entirely** — the post-detection deletion-ratio trigger in §2.2 still catches major restructures even without an audit pass.
165	
166	2. **Parse the report for an "Out-of-Scope Observations" section.** Look for either a top-level `## Out-of-Scope Observations` heading or a `### Out-of-Scope New Public API` subsection under `## Remediation Suggestions`. Each entry must expose:
167	
168	   - `path` — literal file path or directory glob (e.g., `python/cocoindex/_internal/api.py` or `python/cocoindex/resources/**`)
169	   - `evidence` — short one-liner from the report (export count, rationale)
170	
171	   **Note:** This section is an optional audit-skill output. `skf-audit-skill` does not currently discover new files (per `src/skf-audit-skill/references/re-index.md` — new-file detection is the responsibility of update-skill). The section is a forward-looking integration point: manual additions to the drift report or a future audit-skill enhancement populate it. If absent, no candidates from this trigger — proceed to step 6.
172	
173	3. **Reconcile against existing amendments.** For each candidate, consult `brief.scope.amendments[]`:
174	
175	   - `action: "promoted"` AND `path` matches → already in scope, skip silently.
176	   - `action: "skipped"` AND `path` matches → user previously declined, honor silently.
177	   - `action: "demoted-include"` or `action: "demoted-exclude"` AND `path` matches → user previously narrowed scope on this path, do not re-prompt; record as `pre_decided`.
178	   - No matching amendment → continue to user prompt.
179	
180	4. **Prompt for each unresolved candidate.** Present the same menu shape as §1b:
181	
182	   ```
183	   **Out-of-scope new public API discovered**
184	
185	   Path:          {candidate.path}
186	   Evidence:      {evidence from drift report}
187	   Drift report:  {report relative path}
188	
189	   This path was not in the brief's `scope.include` when the skill was created. How should update-skill handle it?
190	
191	   [P] Promote — add to scope.include AND extract in this run
192	   [S] Skip    — leave out of scope AND record skip in amendments (no re-prompt)
193	   [U] Update  — halt this run and return to skf-brief-skill to refine scope
194	   ```
195	
196	5. **Headless mode (`{headless_mode}` is true):** auto-select `[S] Skip` for every candidate — record `action: "skipped"`, `category: "scope-expansion"`, `reason: "headless: no user to prompt"`, `workflow: "skf-update-skill"`. A non-interactive update run must never silently expand scope.
197	
198	6. **Apply decision:**
199	
200	   - **[P] Promote:**
201	     1. Append `candidate.path` to `brief.scope.include` as a literal glob (preserve any wildcards from the drift report).
202	     2. Append a `brief.scope.amendments[]` entry: `action: "promoted"`, `category: "scope-expansion"`, `path: candidate.path`, `reason: {user-provided or auto: "out-of-scope new public API — drift report {report basename}"}`, `evidence: {evidence string}`, `date: {today ISO}`, `workflow: "skf-update-skill"`.
203	     3. **Write the amended brief back to disk immediately** at `{forge_data_folder}/{skill_name}/skill-brief.yaml`. Preserve all other fields.
204	     4. Display: `"Promoted {path} — brief amended; §2 Category A will pick up matching files as ADDED."`
205	     5. **No `promoted_docs_new[]` entry and no `change_detection_excludes` write** — promoted code globs flow through the standard §2 Category A → §3 extraction path, unlike §1b's promoted docs which bypass extraction.
206	
207	   - **[S] Skip:**
208	     1. Do NOT modify `scope.include` or `scope.exclude`.
209	     2. Append a `brief.scope.amendments[]` entry: `action: "skipped"`, `category: "scope-expansion"`, `path: candidate.path`, `reason: {user-provided or auto: "user declined promotion at update-skill §1c"}`, `evidence: {evidence string}`, `date: {today ISO}`, `workflow: "skf-update-skill"`.
210	     3. **Write the amended brief back to disk** so neither §1c nor a future run will re-prompt.
211	     4. Display: `"Skipped {path} — decision recorded in amendments."`
212	
213	   - **[U] Update:**
214	     1. Halt the workflow immediately.
215	     2. Display: `"Halting update-skill. Re-run skf-brief-skill to refine scope for {skill_name}, then re-run skf-update-skill."`
216	     3. Exit with status `halted-for-brief-refinement`. Change manifest is not yet built — no partial writes to provenance.
217	
218	7. **Summary:** After all candidates are resolved (or none were found):
219	
220	   - `"Scope reconciliation: {N} candidates, {P} promoted, {S} skipped, {A} pre-decided from amendments."`
221	   - If N = 0 (section absent or empty): `"Scope reconciliation: no out-of-scope observations in drift report."`
222	   - If §1c was skipped entirely (no drift report): omit this line; §2.2 will still run.
223	
224	**Record for evidence report:** the update-skill evidence report appends `scope_reconciliation_pre: {drift_report: path, candidates: N, promoted: P, skipped: S, pre_decided: A, decisions: [{path, action, evidence}]}` (omit when §1c was skipped).

227

229	
230	#### 2.0 — Build Pre-filter Exclusion Set
231	
232	Before launching parallel subprocesses, build a `change_detection_excludes` set in context that Category A subprocess workers must honor. Parallel subprocesses cannot see each other's in-memory state, so any coordination between §1b's decisions and §2's scan results must be pre-materialized into an explicit input the subprocesses receive.
233	
234	The exclusion set includes:
235	
236	- Every path in `promoted_docs_new[]` (populated by §1b). These files are tracked as `file_entries[]` via step 4 Priority 7, not through Category A code extraction. Without this exclusion, Category A would classify them as ADDED (because they're in source but not yet in the provenance map) and §3 re-extract would send them to AST extraction, producing ghost entries.
237	- Every source path in `file_entries[].source_file` where `file_type == "doc"` in the existing provenance map. These are already-tracked authoritative docs; any drift in them is handled by Category D (script/asset file changes), not Category A.
238	
239	Record the set size: "**Change-detection excludes:** {count} paths ({promoted_docs_new count} new promotions + {existing doc file_entries count} already tracked)."

Suggestions\n    in_remediation = False\n    for i, line in enumerate(lines):\n        if _REMEDIATION_HEADING.match(line):\n            in_remediation = True\n            continue\n        if in_remediation and _ANY_TOP_LEVEL_HEADING.match(line):\n            in_remediation = False\n            continue\n        if in_remediation and _NESTED_HEADING.match(line):\n            return _gather_until_next_heading(lines, i + 1, _ANY_SUB_LEVEL_HEADING)\n\n    return None\n\n\ndef _gather_until_next_heading(\n    lines: list[str], start: int, stop_pattern: re.Pattern[str]\n) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Collect lines from `start` until the next heading matching stop_pattern.\"\"\"\n    out: list[str] = []\n    for i in range(start, len(lines)):\n        if stop_pattern.match(lines[i]):\n            break\n        out.append(lines[i])\n    return \"\\n\".join(out).strip()\n\n\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Parse candidates from the section text\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\n# Bullet-list shape: \"- `path/to/thing` — evidence text\"\n# (em-dash, en-dash, or plain hyphen as separator)\n_BULLET = re.compile(\n    r\"^\\s*[-*]\\s+`(?P<path>[^`]+)`\\s*[—–-]\\s*(?P<evidence>.+?)\\s*$\"\n)\n\n# Table shape: \"| path | evidence |\"\n_TABLE_ROW = re.compile(\n    r\"^\\|\\s*`?(?P<path>[^|`]+?)`?\\s*\\|\\s*(?P<evidence>[^|]+?)\\s*\\|\"\n)\n_TABLE_SEPARATOR = re.compile(r\"^\\|\\s*[-:]+\\s*\\|\")\n\n\ndef parse_candidates(section_text: str) -> list[dict]:\n    \"\"\"Extract (path, evidence) candidates from an Out-of-Scope section.\n\n    Recognized formats:\n      - Bullet lines: `- \\`path/to\\` — evidence`\n      - Markdown table: `| path | evidence |` (skip header/separator rows)\n    \"\"\"\n    if not section_text:\n        return []\n    candidates: list[dict] = []\n    in_table = False\n    table_header_seen = False\n    for line in section_text.splitlines():\n        stripped = line.strip()\n        if not stripped:\n            in_table = False\n            table_header_seen = False\n            continue\n\n        if _TABLE_SEPARATOR.match(stripped):\n            in_table = True\n            table_header_seen = True\n            continue\n\n        if stripped.startswith(\"|\"):\n            if not table_header_seen:\n                # First table-shaped line is the header — skip\n                table_header_seen = True\n                continue\n            m = _TABLE_ROW.match(stripped)\n            if m:\n                path = m.group(\"path\").strip()\n                evidence = m.group(\"evidence\").strip()\n                if path and not _looks_like_table_header(path):\n                    candidates.append({\"path\": path, \"evidence\": evidence})\n            continue\n\n        m = _BULLET.match(line)\n        if m:\n            candidates.append(\n                {\n                    \"path\": m.group(\"path\").strip(),\n                    \"evidence\": m.group(\"evidence\").strip(),\n                }\n            )\n    return candidates\n\n\ndef _looks_like_table_header(text: str) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"True if `text` looks like a table-header cell label (e.g. 'path',\n    'evidence'). Headers slip past `_TABLE_SEPARATOR` only when the report\n    uses a header row without the canonical `|---|---|` separator.\"\"\"\n    return text.lower() in {\"path\", \"evidence\", \"file\", \"files\", \"candidate\", \"rationale\"}\n\n\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Reconcile candidates against brief.scope.amendments[]\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\n_ALREADY_IN_SCOPE = \"already-in-scope\"\n_PRE_DECIDED_SKIPPED = \"pre-decided-skipped\"\n_PRE_DECIDED_DEMOTED = \"pre-decided-demoted\"\n_UNRESOLVED = \"unresolved\"\n\n\ndef load_brief(brief_path: Path) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Parse a skill-brief.yaml file. Raises ValueError on load failure.\"\"\"\n    try:\n        text = brief_path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    except OSError as exc:\n        raise ValueError(f\"cannot read brief at {brief_path}: {exc}\") from exc\n    try:\n        brief = yaml.safe_load(text)\n    except yaml.YAMLError as exc:\n        raise ValueError(f\"brief at {brief_path} is not valid YAML: {exc}\") from exc\n    if not isinstance(brief, dict):\n        raise ValueError(\n            f\"brief at {brief_path} must be a YAML mapping, got \"\n            f\"{type(brief).__name__}\"\n        )\n    return brief\n\n\ndef reconcile(candidates: list[dict], brief: dict) -> list[dict]:\n    \"\"\"Classify each candidate against brief.scope.amendments[].\"\"\"\n    scope = brief.get(\"scope\")\n    amendments = []\n    if isinstance(scope, dict):\n        amendments = scope.get(\"amendments\") or []\n    if not isinstance(amendments, list):\n        amendments = []\n\n    # index amendments by path → list of actions (most recent first preserved)\n    by_path: dict[str, list[str]] = {}\n    for amend in amendments:\n        if not isinstance(amend, dict):\n            continue\n        path = amend.get(\"path\")\n        action = amend.get(\"action\")\n        if isinstance(path, str) and isinstance(action, str):\n            by_path.setdefault(path, []).append(action)\n\n    classified: list[dict] = []\n    for candidate in candidates:\n        path = candidate[\"path\"]\n        evidence = candidate.get(\"evidence\", \"\")\n        prior_actions = by_path.get(path, [])\n        status, prior_action = _classify(prior_actions)\n        classified.append(\n            {\n                \"path\": path,\n                \"evidence\": evidence,\n                \"status\": status,\n                \"prior_action\": prior_action,\n            }\n        )\n    return classified\n\n\ndef _classify(prior_actions: list[str]) -> tuple[str, str | None]:\n    \"\"\"Pick the dominant amendment action for a single candidate path.\n\n    A path may have multiple amendments (e.g. promoted then later\n    demoted-exclude). Most recent action wins — the list is in\n    amendment-record-insertion order, so iterate from the end.\n    \"\"\"\n    for action in reversed(prior_actions):\n        if action == \"promoted\":\n            return _ALREADY_IN_SCOPE, \"promoted\"\n        if action == \"skipped\":\n            return _PRE_DECIDED_SKIPPED, \"skipped\"\n        if action in (\"demoted-include\", \"demoted-exclude\"):\n            return _PRE_DECIDED_DEMOTED, action\n    return _UNRESOLVED, None\n\n\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Dispatch: orchestrate all three steps\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef dispatch(\n    *,\n    forge_data_folder: Path,\n    skill_name: str,\n    baseline_version: str,\n    brief_path: Path,\n) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Run the full §1c discovery + parse + reconcile pipeline.\"\"\"\n    report = discover_drift_report(forge_data_folder, skill_name, baseline_version)\n    if report is None:\n        return {\n            \"status\": \"no-report\",\n            \"report_path\": None,\n            \"candidates_total\": 0,\n            \"classified\": [],\n            \"summary\": {\"pre_decided_count\": 0, \"unresolved_count\": 0},\n        }\n\n    text = report.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    section = extract_out_of_scope_section(text)\n    if section is None:\n        return {\n            \"status\": \"no-candidates\",\n            \"report_path\": str(report),\n            \"candidates_total\": 0,\n            \"classified\": [],\n            \"summary\": {\"pre_decided_count\": 0, \"unresolved_count\": 0},\n        }\n\n    candidates = parse_candidates(section)\n    if not candidates:\n        return {\n            \"status\": \"no-candidates\",\n            \"report_path\": str(report),\n            \"candidates_total\": 0,\n            \"classified\": [],\n            \"summary\": {\"pre_decided_count\": 0, \"unresolved_count\": 0},\n        }\n\n    brief = load_brief(brief_path)\n    classified = reconcile(candidates, brief)\n\n    pre_decided = sum(1 for c in classified if c[\"status\"] != _UNRESOLVED)\n    unresolved = sum(1 for c in classified if c[\"status\"] == _UNRESOLVED)\n\n    return {\n        \"status\": \"candidates-found\",\n        \"report_path\": str(report),\n        \"candidates_total\": len(classified),\n        \"classified\": classified,\n        \"summary\": {\n            \"pre_decided_count\": pre_decided,\n            \"unresolved_count\": unresolved,\n        },\n    }\n\n\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# CLI\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef _cmd_dispatch(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:\n    forge = Path(args.forge_data_folder)\n    if not forge.is_dir():\n        print(\n            f\"error: forge-data-folder not a directory: {forge}\", file=sys.stderr\n        )\n        return 1\n    brief_path = Path(args.brief)\n    if not brief_path.is_file():\n        print(f\"error: brief not found: {brief_path}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return 1\n    try:\n        result = dispatch(\n            forge_data_folder=forge,\n            skill_name=args.skill_name,\n            baseline_version=args.baseline_version,\n            brief_path=brief_path,\n        )\n    except ValueError as exc:\n        print(f\"error: {exc}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return 1\n    json.dump(result, sys.stdout, indent=2)\n    sys.stdout.write(\"\\n\")\n    return 0\n\n\ndef _build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(\n        prog=\"skf-provenance-gap-dispatch\",\n        description=(\n            \"Locate the latest drift report, extract Out-of-Scope candidates, \"\n            \"and classify them against brief.scope.amendments[].\"\n        ),\n    )\n    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest=\"cmd\", required=True)\n\n    p = sub.add_parser(\"dispatch\", help=\"run the full §1c pipeline\")\n    p.add_argument(\"--skill-name\", required=True)\n    p.add_argument(\"--baseline-version\", required=True)\n    p.add_argument(\"--forge-data-folder\", required=True)\n    p.add_argument(\"--brief\", required=True, help=\"path to skill-brief.yaml\")\n    p.set_defaults(func=_cmd_dispatch)\n\n    return parser\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    parser = _build_parser()\n    args = parser.parse_args(argv)\n    return args.func(args)\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    raise SystemExit(main())\n"
